#4217. Cozy Magical Sim Witchbrook Gets A January Release Date

Witchbrook is a game I've been looking forward to for a while, and today's Nintendo Indie World showcase finally confirmed the game's release date: January 28. Any game from Chucklefish, best known for publishing Stardew Valley and developing the Wargroove series, is worthy of my attention, and Witchbrook looks more exciting the more we see of it. See it for yourself in the release date trailer below.

The game mixes cute pixel art with a robust suite of magical gameplay systems. As you go to a witch college to learn spells, you'll also build a life in the town, making friends, working jobs, decorating your home, and more. It was an appealing pitch when it was announced nearly 10 years ago in 2017, and it remains so to this day. After a long stretch of relative silence, last year the game was scheduled to launch sometime in 2026. Obviously, the team has faced some delays since then, but we're just glad it's actually coming out.

Witchbrook's release date was announced during today's Nintendo-specific stream, but it's coming to all major platforms: PS5, Xbox Series X/S, Switch 2, Switch, and PC.

Last week, we took a look at two very different covers for NSO newbie Avenging Spirit on the Game Boy. The disparate designs did the North American variant no favours, as it wound up with only 30% of the vote, leaving the cuter Japanese and European cover to take the remaining 70%.

#4214. Nintendo Indie World Showcase Recap: Everything We Saw

The year is nearing its conclusion, and the last big AAA titles are rolling out one-by-one. But today, it was all about the independent titles on Nintendo's latest Indie World Showcase, highlighting new games from smaller indie teams coming to the Switch and Switch 2.

Here's everything we saw at the October 2026 Nintendo Indie World Showcase.

Today's Indie World Showcase started with a big headliner, as the long-awaited witch-life simulator Witchbrook got a release date. Chucklefish and Robtality's cozy magical world goes live on January 28, 2027.

Fans of 3D platformers should probably keep an eye on Winds of Viridia, which looks like a colorful game with a lot of interesting movement and exploration. Shark Jump's fantastical platformer is arriving next year, but if the wait's too long, a free demo is coming today on the eShop.

From one of the co-creators of Celeste, City of None has a gorgeous pixelated art style and colors that immediately remind me of Game Boy Color classics. It's a 2D platformer where you leap around, fight enemies, and explore the strange city around you. The jumping and fighting look solid, and I really like the mysterious atmosphere and art direction. City of None's set for sometime in 2027.

The sword-surfing adventure from the makers of Abzu and Journey is coming to Nintendo Switch 2 on October 29, 2026 - tomorrow! It's a gorgeous adventure that earned a Must-Play badge from us, so it's worth your time if you like the kinds of gorgeous, beautiful adventures Giant Squid (developer of Abzu) is known for.

Take an overhead camera angle, brawler gameplay, and some John Wick sensibilities, and you've got Tenjutsu, a stylish roguelike where you use your martial arts prowess to tear apart crime syndicates. I really enjoy the look and vibe of this one, and it's from one of the designers of Dead Cells, too. Tenjutsu might be one to keep an eye on when it arrives on Switch 2 in 2027.

RPG fans have been eating well, and it looks like the feast could continue next year with Threads of Time. The time-traveling RPG is coming to both Switch and Switch 2 next summer, and it's looking absolutely gorgeous.

Ah, raccoons. Nature's most adorable little scamps. If you and your friends have ever wanted to live out the dream of being a rambunctious band of raccoons wreaking havoc on the town, Dumpster Gang sets out to give you just that fantasy in March 2027.

I've already enjoyed quite a bit of Super Battle Golf on PC, so I'll tell you now: if you enjoy golf games and want some Mario Party annoy-your-friends antics wound around them, Super Battle Golf should be on your radar for its March 25, 2027 launch on Switch 2.

Another port of a PC multiplayer mainstay, the co-op physics-driven horror-looter R.E.P.O. is coming to Switch 2 in 2027. This is one for the crowd that likes to be scared one moment and laughing hysterically the next.

Rounding out the co-op section, Haunted Paws has you and a pal playing as a pair of pups searching for their person in a haunted mansion. The side-scrolling 3D look makes it seem like a less-scary Little Nightmares, and the concept is pretty fun. Look for this one on Switch and Switch 2 in May 2027, or try out the free demo later today.

Enjoy shrines, towns, and strange night-time journeys into the unknown? Follow a fox girl and her frog friend on an adventure through a strange island in Kitsune: The Journey of Adashino on Switch 2 and Switch in spring 2027. I've said it a few times in this recap, but wow, the art here is great.

The second entry in the slime-collecting, home-building sim adventure is coming to Switch 2. Pick up adorable slimes with your vacuum, build a home for them, and explore the Rainbow Island around you in January 2027. Plus, there's an exclusive in-game item for the Switch 2 version.

From the makers of Cozy Grove, this multiplayer game encourages players to build a home above the clouds with friends and explore the world around them. Spirit Crossing looks like a big world to make your own alongside your pals, starting November 16, 2026 on both Switch and Switch 2.

Want something a little sillier? My Arms Are Longer Now is a game about, well, really long arms. With numerous Australian comedians lending their vocal talents to the project, this seems like it could be a quirky, charming, and delightfully funny experience when it arrives on both Switch and Switch 2 on March 11, 2027.

The delightfully Game Boy-styled critter delivery game Petal Runner is aiming for a full launch. I've played a bit of this one at events over the years, and it's charmed me every time. If you like nostalgic adventures with a surprisingly heartfelt core, you should mark down the March 8, 2027 launch, or check out the free demo arriving later today.

The chaotic coin-pushing game Raccoin is coming to Nintendo Switch 2. It's just like those token-shoving games you remember from arcades but with a number of wild and wacky means of pushing even more coins over the edge run-over-run. Raccoin: Chaos Max Edition hits Switch 2 on November 10, 2026, and a free demo is out later today.

#4213. Battlefield 6 is getting a free trial next week with a decent selection of maps and modes

Battlefield 6's second-ever free trial, and the first in 2026, is upon us.

Battlefield Studios has announced that Battlefield 6 is going free to play for one week next week. Well, a portion of the game is, anyway, as part of a free trial that will include some of the game’s most popular modes and maps.

Though it does not encompass the entirety of the game, the free trial is fairly generous. Here’s what to expect.

For starters, the trial kicks off Tuesday, March 17 and will run until the following Tuesday, March 24. The trial will be accessible from Battlefield Redsec, the already free-to-play portion of the game.

Once downloaded, you’ll find a new Battlefield 6 Free Trial section in the main menu. Because Redsec and Battlefield 6 multiplayer share progression, if you played the former at any point, you’ll be able to pick up from where you left off.

The same is also true the other way around; if this is your first time with Battlefield 6, all your unlocks will carry over to the full version, as well as to Redsec if you decide stick with the free-to-play off-shoot.

Once it kicks off, you’ll find three playlists to choose from. Casual Breakthrough, All-out Warfare, and a third playlist showcasing the new Nightfall game mode and its associated map.

All-out Warfare is what you come to Battlefield for, and that playlist features Conquest, Breakthrough, as well as BF6’s newcomer Escalation - all large-scale, combined arms game modes. They will be playable across four maps. You get to play on two from Season 2: Contaminated, and Hagental Base, one from Season 1: Eastwood, and Mirak Valley from the base game.

Casual Breakthrough is based on a playlist that already exists in the core game, and it’s really designed as a nice on-ramp for new players. It also offers less intense gameplay, perfect for people grinding unlocks.

Casual Breakthrough is limited to just 16 real players (eight per team), with the rest filled up with bots. You earn the same amount of XP in those matches, except when you interact with bots, so killing a bot will net less than a human player. Outside of that, unlocks, Challenges and all other things that don’t depend on stat-tracking can be done within.

In the trial, the Casual Breakthrough playlist includes Hagental Base, Contaminated, and Eastwood.

The most interesting is the third playlist, in part because its content will also be available to owners of the full game for the first time right alongside free-to-play players. Nightfall is a playlist exclusive to the Hagental Base map.

This is a very small map, so the mode selection here is Team Deathmatch, Squad Deathmatch, and Domination. Under Nightfall conditions, lights across the entire map are turned off, so you’re going to have use your NVGs to be able to see. This is also a god opportunity to try out weapon attachments that specifically work under low-light conditions, which typically don’t get much use in multiplayer.

March 17 also marks the launch of the second stage of Battlefield 6’s Season 2, which comes with the aforementioned Nightfall content, as well as a big new update - so the timing works out nicely for everyone.

#4212. Feature: Nintendo Life eShop Selects (October 2026)

The best eShop games on Switch 1 & 2 in October

There have been a lot of them this month — too many to play, in fact. So if you're looking for the cream of the crop, and specifically the good video games on eShop that you can't (yet) buy in any physical form, you've come to the right place.

We've got six games this month that scored at least 7/10 in time for this showdown (and a couple more reviews in the oven which may qualify but aren't quite past the finish line at the time of writing).

As a reminder, these are Switch eShop games that don't have physical releases — which includes Game-Key Cards or codes-in-boxes — at the time of writing.

Our writers and contributors have voted for their top three eShop games of October 2026 and this is the result.

Before we get to the trio of podium places, let's see the other contenders:

Kicking off our top trio of appropriately spooky releases, we've got Wrong Organ's Mouthwashing. Coming to consoles a couple of years after its PC debut, we had heard great things — great and disturbing things — and we weren't disappointed.

"Simply put, Mouthwashing is a game best played when you’re lost in its grim setting, feeling like you, too, are stuck on the Tulpar and living this nightmare," wrote Rhiannon. "Its rich horror is found in every corner of the game and through every tool at the devs’ disposal. So it stands to reason that making it even easier to get lost in Mouthwashing — without sitting at your PC — only helps the game sink its teeth into you."

If you're looking for something great (and, indeed, disturbing) to play over Halloween, get this downloaded.

There's a Game-Key Card release coming, but not until next year. Therefore, RE4make REm4ke Resident Evil 4 Gold Edition takes its deserved second-place spot on the eShop Selects podium this month.

Ollie called it "the gold standard for modern remakes" in his review. "It updates the original beautifully, remaining faithful yet improving upon almost every element. The combat feels weighty and satisfying, the locations have all been expanded upon without feeling bloated, and there's enough content here to keep you coming back for years." If only we had that sort of time!

However, RE was held off the top spot this month by something similarly creepy though very different...

Spooky Doorway's The Séance of Blake Manor launched to critical acclaim on PC in 2025, and turned up on consoles exactly one year on, just in time for All Hallow's Eve. Again. And we were very glad to see it.

Especially Roland, who gave it a 9/10 and called it "something special" in his review, but it's evidently had the same effect on the rest of Team NL.

"Its broad cast of characters, vivid writing and engaging voice performances make it akin to curling up with an interactive, supernatural Agatha Christie novel – one that will spook you just enough for a cosy Halloween."

If you haven't tried this elsewhere, we urge you to give it a go now. Not even the lack of mouse controls puts a dint in it.

< Nintendo eShop Selects - September 2026

Do you agree with our ranking? Tell us about your favourite eShop releases of last month by voting in our poll and sharing your thoughts in the comments.

How we decide our eShop Selects top three: As we reach the end of every month, the Nintendo Life staff vote on their favourite titles from a list of games selected by the editorial team. To qualify for this list, these games must have been released as a digital-only Nintendo Switch eShop title in that particular month, and must have been reviewed on Nintendo Life; we select the qualifying games based on their review scores.

Staff are then asked to vote for three games that they think deserve to sit right at the very top of that list; first choice gets three points, second choice gets two points, and third choice gets one point. These votes are then tallied to create a top-three list, with the overall winner taking that month's top prize.

#4211. Phantom Blade Zero: Here's How To Get The Perfect Ending, Which Is The Only Satisfying One

Phantom Blade Zero is a sprawling Wuxia adventure, the best action game of the year, and one of my favorite action games ever. It offers a lot to do, from main story quests to dozens of side quests, collectibles, hidden bosses, secret areas, and more. I highly recommend checking out Game Informer's list of Phantom Blade Zero tips and tricks before jumping in. It mentions some tasks required to achieve the perfect ending, but here I'll break down exactly what you need to see it.

As a note, getting the perfect ending in Phantom Blade Zero isn't that unreasonable. It requires doing a lot of the game's side content, but it's not shrouded in mystery or puzzles; you just need to complete certain things before heading into the finale. I'm going to keep these requirements relatively spoiler-free, and honestly, without the wider story context, they'll be a lot of mumbo jumbo proper nouns that don't really mean anything. If you're set on getting the perfect ending, I'd bookmark this page, and as you play Phantom Blade Zero, more and more of these requirements will start to make sense. However, if you think even a name or proper noun is a spoiler, be careful reading these requirements.

The following requirements don't necessarily have a set order. You could technically ignore all of this and then go after everything right before the game's "last chance to get things done" warning near the finale. So don't sweat about picking up this or that at a certain time in your journey – do it when you want to. Just make sure you have the following requirements completed before heading past the "last chance" warning.

For more, read Game Informer's Phantom Blade Zero tips and tricks, and then read Game Informer's Phantom Blade Zero review.

#4210. Turn 10 Director Departs Microsoft As Forza Studio Merges With Playground Games

After 27 years, Dan Greenawalt retires from Microsoft

Dan Greenawalt is leaving Turn 10 Studios after 27 years, as the Forza Motorsport developer merges into Playground Games and is officially renamed Playground Games Redmond.

Greenawalt was there from day dot for Team Green, shipping original Xbox title Project Gotham Racing in 2001 before going onto to lead the creation of Forza, founding Turn 10 Studios, and publishing eight phenomenal racing games.

Reported by The Verge's Tom Warren, Playground Games Studio head Trevor Williams shared an internal memo with his team that "Dan Greenawalt has decided that this is the right time for him to retire from Microsoft,".

"It’s hard to overstate Dan’s impact over the past 27 years. From shipping Project Gotham Racing on the original XBOX in 2001 to leading the creation of Forza, founding Turn 10 Studios and appearing so many times on our E3 stage, usually making a dramatic entrance with a supercar in tow – and so much more – we owe tremendous thanks and gratitude to Dan. On behalf of both teams, I would like to thank Dan for his leadership, his support, and his partnership. I wish him well for whatever comes next."

With Greenawalt retiring from Microsoft, and Turn 10 spun into Playground Games Redmond, the team is now helping with the development of Forza Horizon and Fable.

#4209. Phantom Blade Zero Has Secret Upgrades In NG+

Sam Woods is TheGamer’s Senior Reporter. He’s been in games journalism since 2020 and has undertaken a variety of roles in that time. These have included roles such as SEO Editor, Managing Editor at DualShockers, and Global Head of Gaming, and he's also been seen on the BBC. He was promoted to the Senior Reporter position in 2025 following a series of high-quality reports and exclusives for TheGamer.

Since 2020, Sam has written over 3,000 articles and specializes in telling the stories of the people behind the games. He’s interviewed the biggest game directors, some of the industry’s top talents, told the stories of how indie games came to be, and spoken to players about what really makes them tick. He’s also interviewed some of the world’s biggest musical artists to find out how the medium has inspired their work, and TV and Film actors about their roles in video game adaptations. He even hosted a PAX panel in 2021 and made a documentary in 2024 surrounding the creation of a Disney game.

Alongside this, Sam focuses on breaking news. He got the scoop on Perfect Dark’s cancellation, provided context on some AI drama, and revealed that Lady Dimitrescu’s actress would love to step back into the character’s giant shoes. These articles have been picked up by the biggest gaming sites, including IGN, GameSpot, and PC Gamer. He also loves to dive into the numbers behind the games.

Sam’s journey in games journalism has taken him all over the world. He’s covered Gamescom in Germany, Summer Game Fest in Los Angeles, and Tokyo Game Show in Japan, each on three occasions.

He’s been learning Japanese since 2024 with the intention of identifying and translating Japanese-language news and bringing it to English-language audiences first, something he’s done countless times.

Sam’s first review was 2020’s Battletoads reboot, and he’s since reviewed games in The Legend of Zelda, Super Mario, and Pokemon franchises.

Phantom Blade Zero has a vast, vast array of build options. 30 weapons are accompanied by a further 30 Phantom Edges, with a bunch of accessories and medicines to really spice things up. 30 is the magic number, as on your first playthrough, you can upgrade your weapons and Phantom Edges to level 30.

There's always a fear that, when you start a second playthrough, weapon and equipment levels stay capped. Thankfully, that's not the case in Phantom Blade Zero, but you still have a unique hurdle to clear if you want to upgrade weapons past their cap in New Game+.

I'm lucky enough to have had the game for a while now, scoring it a 5/5 in my review. I've completed it twice and am now confident in what I feel are the game's 10 Best Weapons and 10 Best Phantom Edges. It wasn't until I was a little way through my second playthrough, though, that I realized that they could be upgraded past their level 30 cap.

I began my second playthrough using the Crescent Blade, my favorite weapon in the game, and the Blazing Edge, the Soul Tempered version of the Sanguine Reach. I checked at the first Bell to see whether I could upgrade them—I couldn't—so I continued my adventure expecting that, in the later stages, I might feel a little underpowered.

I eventually reached the first Mandate Outpost in Weeping Creek Valley, spoke to the blacksmith, and collected another version of the Sanguine Reach, so I decided to check the weapon upgrade screen again. This time, I could upgrade my Blazing Edge. It turns out you can upgrade your weapons and Phantom Edges on NG+ after you've found them on your second playthrough.

I quickly realized I could upgrade any accessory I found again by +1. This often kept their base bonus the same, adding a 3% boost to a random stat like attack power or total Sha-Chi. Unfortunately, Medicines are the only items whose first-playthrough cap carries over into NG+.

These upgrades are easily missed, but can certainly help you turn the tide on the Maskwalkers in any subsequent playthroughs.

#4207. Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.1 livestream reveals a pared-back, four-week update as HoYo plays catch-up

Honkai: Star Rail will continue the Planarcadia story arc in Version 4.1, as the Star Rail Fest presents a new twist.

A new Honkai: Star Rail Special Program has concluded, which means some fresh news about the game’s upcoming major update. Version 4.1, unveiled today as Unraveled for Daybreak, is the action RPG’s next moment, kicking off on March 25.

Unraveled for Daybreak is the next chapter in the ongoing story of Planarcadia, with the Astra Express Crew now invited to a fan fest inspired by their own past journeys. The aptly named Star Rail Fest is ostensibly hosted to allow more of the citizens of Arcadia to experience the Trailblaze.

As everyone’s eyes is fixated on the grand Star Rail Fest, the Phantasmoon Games continue to be in full swing, as does the war with the Supplicants. Star Rail Fest is, however, the big focus of this update, in case it wasn't obvious.

The event is made up of three large-scale zones, each themed around past excursions of the Astral Express. You’ll get to explore the Belobog Zone, Xianzhou Luofu Zone, and Penacony Zone. Later on, you’ll also be able to visit Pearluxe Tower, the headquarters of Pearluxe Corp.

Each area will feature its own attractions, such as the balloon figures of Supreme Guardian Cocolia and the Destruction Engine, the duel against the Lord Ravager Phantylia at Scalegorge Waterscape, and the Pearluxe Tower’s Alloy King Pom-Pom model.

The hot new arrival is bumbling noirish detective Ashveil whom we've met in Version 4.0, and who becomes a playable character with this update. Ashveil is a 5-Star Lightning-Type character, on the Path of The Hunt. You’ll be able to pull for him throughout 4.1's runtime, which is slightly reduced at four weeks instead of the usual six, in order to rebalance the schedule after the extra-long Version 3.8.

In combat, Ashveil is capable of increasing Crit Damage of all allies. He can also mark an enemy as Bait, which reduces the Defence of all enemies on the field so long as this tag holds. If Ashveil uses his Skill on the baited target, he will deal extra Damage and regain Skill Points for the team.

Ashveil can bully that baited target even further by launching Hounding Pursuit. If any of his teammates attacks the Bait, he can further deliver a follow-up attack that gradually accumulates Gluttony for as long as he’s in combat. Gluttony can later be consumed to boost follow-up attack damage.

If he lands a kill, Ashveil continues to deal damage to the next enemy he attacks. That buff is transferred if that enemy is killed. Even in map exploration, Ashveil can be deadly, capable of inflicting Stunned upon enemies within a specific range.

Returning characters this patch will be Hyacine in the first half, and Boothill in the second half. Once again, due to the reduced runtime, their banner reruns will be slightly shorter than normal, at just two weeks each instead of three — so be sure to take that into account if you're planning on pulling for either of them.

Version 4.1 also adds the Wispae War Saga, a new activity where you can practice your leadership skills by commanding different types of Wispae Soldiers in the Graphia Academy. You can upgrade each one, use spell cards to alter their effects, and later face other champions. You ultimately want to play this to unlock new Wispae Companions, not to mention complete the challenges within.

Finally, Version 4.1 marks the start of a new Arcadian Chronicles phase in the Divergent Universe. You’ll be able to use Waypoint Pass cards to explore the different areas. HoYo is also bringing back Planar Fissure and Garden of Plenty with double rewards. And as ever, if you log in for at least seven days after downloading the new patch, you’ll earn 10 premium banner pulls.

#4206. Here's What The Metro Redux Next-Gen Upgrades Look Like On Xbox Series X|S

Last night, we covered the story about Metro 2033 Redux and Metro Last Light Redux getting free upgrades for Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S, and now we've also got some footage of them to bring your way.

This is provided by the YouTube channel Fuzion Xbox Testing, as is typically the case, and it reveals some interesting details that we weren't previously aware of, such as how the two upgrades look and perform on Xbox Series S.

So, with Metro 2033 Redux, we're getting an output of 4K in both the 60FPS and 120FPS modes on Xbox Series X. The 60FPS mode seems to dip into the 50s and even 40s sometimes, but the 120FPS mode appears largely stable according to this initial footage. In both cases, it looks a fantastic upgrade from a visual perspective.

The Xbox Series S version, meanwhile, seems to run at 1080p and at a mostly solid 60FPS.

News Two Metro Redux Games Receive Free 4K/60FPS Upgrades For Xbox Series X|S, Full Patch Notes Revealed

With Metro Last Light Redux, we're getting basically the same situation - two 4K modes at 60FPS and 120FPS on Xbox Series X, although the footage for this game suggests the frame rates are even more stable.

Xbox Series S is once again 1080p at 60FPS, and appears to run extremely well overall.

We're going to leave you with the raw footage for both of these games below, so you can get an idea of what to expect from the free upgrades. If you haven't played them before (or in a long time), it might be worth starting now!

Are you playing the new versions of Metro Redux on Xbox Series X or Series S? Tell us down below.

The evil Ganondorf is scheming to steal the mythical Triforce from the Sacred Realm and take over the world. Now Link must become the hero of time and save the kingdom in this classic tale, built from the ground up for the Nintendo Switch 2 system.

Pre-Order The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Nintendo Switch 2

Guide Where To Pre-Order The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time & Zelda Nintendo Switch 2 Console

Developer Shift Up's third-person action-adventure was well received at launch back in 2024, and we're intrigued to see how it holds up on Switch 2. Initial impressions of the demo raised some questions over the frame-generation tech used to hit 60fps, although the dev has since confirmed that it can be deactivated in the final game.

Pleasantly, the full game is on the cart, too.

Save humanity from extinction in this electrifying, story-driven action-adventure! Step into the boots of EVE, a member of the 7th Airborne Squad sent to reclaim an Earth devastated by mysterious, powerful creatures known as the Naytiba. Engage in razor-sharp, stylish combat as you explore breathtaking post-apocalyptic landscapes, face intense boss encounters, and uncover the dark truths behind humanity’s fall. Optimized for Nintendo Switch 2, experience EVE’s journey at home or on the go, complete with immersive Joy-Con 2 motion controls for activities like fishing. This edition also includes content from the 'Stellar Blade x NieR:Automata' and 'Stellar Blade x GODDESS OF VICTORY: NIKKE' DLCs, as well as a stunning new collaboration with Bayonetta that includes 4 couture outfits for EVE.

Nintendo is still cracking on with Switch 2 Editions of its previous hits, and this update to the last Pikmin game adds some extra Dandori tests plus voice commands for goodboi Oatchi, the closest thing to Nintendogs we'll have until a new Nintendogs.

You can now give voice commands to Oatchi using the built-in microphone on Nintendo Switch 2. Plus, a new mode is blooming: Dandori Academy. Take on challenges and test how quickly you can collect treasure within the stage. Test your Dandori skills and once you’re ready, aim for a high score! Earn medals based on how well you do and see the scores of your friends and players around the world. 72 Dandori Academy stages will be released over time.

A cracking game that we're happy to see finally come to Switch, it released elsewhere in 2024 and proved to be another winner from Atlus. As with all of Sega's Switch 2 output, this one's a Game-Key Card.

Enter the royal tournament to fight for the throne and for the future. Control your destiny, face your fears, and awaken magical “Archetype” powers that lie dormant in your heart. Team up with a compelling cast of characters and embark on an immersive journey that promises hours of captivating exploration, dynamic turn-based with a blend of real-time combat, and exhilarating discovery!

Another Game-Key Card, Rayman returns in a reimagining of his best-selling and last major game. A new version feels a little premature, although Legends did originally come out in 2013, and the included Rayman Origins: Enhanced Edition certainly sweetens the deal.

A bit of a head-scratcher, then, but we're intrigued to see what Ubisoft does to rejig this classic platformer following a last-minute delay from October.

Rayman Legends Retold brings back legendary platforming with new story twists, a brand‑new realm, Kung Foot, and an expanded soundtrack. Sync every move to the beat in unforgettable musical stages, soar across worlds on epic dragon rides, and explore a mysterious new realm in the Glade of Dreams. Play solo or dive into the chaos in up to four‑player couch co‑op, then face off in the fan‑favorite Kung Foot, now bigger and better than ever.

Another Game-Key Card (on Switch 2 - naturally, Switch 1 is getting a regular cart), there's a demo on the eShop for this monster-wrangling DQ spin-off which arrives three years after The Dark Prince. We liked that one well enough, but we're hoping for more from this one.

In this RPG, you befriend monsters from the DRAGON QUEST series, raise them up, synthesize new creatures, and pit them against other monsters in battle. Join fledgling monster wranglers Bianca and Nera as they set off on the adventure of a lifetime.

Capcom's closing out a bumper year with a port of last year's Monster Hunter Wilds. We got our hands on it at TGS and came away impressed - fingers crossed the end product holds up across the board. If you're curious, there's a demo on the eShop right now.

As expected from Capcom, the physical is a Game-Key Card.

The hunt is on! In the latest entry of Capcom's Monster Hunter series, hunt massive monsters in a dynamic, ever-changing world, craft stronger gear, and uncover the mysteries of the Forbidden Lands. Hunt online or together via wireless local play, at home or on the go. Monster Hunter Wilds arrives on Nintendo Switch 2 with full cross-platform play and all Free Title Updates. The massive expansion, Monster Hunter Wilds: Ascendance, is also on the way.

Bringing back the classic Guitar Hero and Rock Band-style rhythm game, Stage Tour has a lot of work to do to convince even fans of those classic games that they need another set of bulky plastic peripherals. We're hoping that developer Red Octane has more than just nostalgia on the setlist.

[Update: It should be noted that the packaging says GAME CARD NOT INCLUDED, confirming that this is a code-in-box job.]

Play your way and take the stage with official Stage Tour hardware or select supported legacy instruments. No instrument controllers required: you can also play with a gamepad or gaming keyboard. Play solo or with up to four players locally, online, or cross-platform, mixing and matching guitar, bass, drums, vocals and Arcade in any combination.

As well as those picks above, there are plenty more Switch 1 & 2 retail games launching in the next couple of months (and a bit beyond).

#4204. Phantom Blade Zero: Longtime Sonic, Ezio Voice Actor Roger Craig Smith Is The New VO For Protagonist Soul

Longtime Sonic the Hedgehog voice actor Roger Craig Smith, who also voices iconic characters such as Ezio Auditore, Chris Redfield, and Batman, is the new voice of Phantom Blade Zero protagonist Soul, according to developer S-Game. Smith replaces former voice actor Jay Maksenuk, who can still be heard voicing Soul in various trailers and gameplay videos.

You can hear Smith's rendition of Soul in the official launch trailer for Phantom Blade Zero, however, below:

Game Informer has reached out to S-Game for a comment or statement on why the VO was changed and will update this story if it learns more.

I can pull back the curtains a bit on how last-minute this change seemingly was for Phantom Blade Zero. For most of my time playing Phantom Blade Zero for review (you can read it here), Soul was still voiced by Maksenuk. I wasn't the biggest fan of the English VO at the time, so I played most of the game using its excellent Chinese VO. However, about a week into the review period for Phantom Blade Zero, developer S-Game told me the VO for Soul had been updated (the team had previously said this update would happen ahead of time).

S-Game didn't say why or who at the time, but after listening to it post-update, it was clear to me it was Smith; his voice is iconic and hard to miss. I was basically at the end of the game at that point, so I didn't get to hear too much, but overall, I like Smith's inclusion as Soul's VO.

Nonetheless, if you're jumping into Phantom Blade Zero at launch, the Soul you play as will be voiced entirely by Smith. Let us know in the comments what you think of it after you've had some time with it!

In the meantime, read Game Informer's Phantom Blade Zero review, and then check out these Phantom Blade Zero tips and tricks.

#4203. Here Are All 10 Star Trek Draft Archetypes In MTG

While it may feel like Magic: The Gathering's Reality Fracture set just dropped yesterday, we have a whole new Universes Beyond drop coming this week, and ahead of the prerelease, we're taking a close look at each Star Trek draft archetype.

There are ten archetypes in total, covering each dual-color combination. The good news is that typically means there is something for every player; you just need to know exactly which mechanics to watch for to build a synergistic deck that will guide you to 3-0 at your prerelease event.

First up is white-blue Spacecrafts & Artifacts, a fairly self-explanatory archetype that leans on Spacecrafts as the main threat, but you first have to plan around stationing them to power up. This means you'll still need to consider creatures as part of your main deck, or ways to consistently create token creatures.

There may, of course, be alternative ways to power up your Spacecrafts that you need to keep an eye on, too. Overall, this may be one of the less-popular archetypes for pre-release, as in a small-deck format it can take too long to get the engine going, and any sign of aggression from your opponents will put you under immense pressure.

This set includes exciting card variants, including the first-ever signed MTG cards, which are sure to be highly valuable.

Not typical of the black-blue archetype, in Star Trek you'll want to lean toward modal choice cards. These cards present you with multiple options and a choice to make either when you resolve the spell or when certain triggers activate. These choices come printed on both creature and noncreature spells, so you can still approach your draft with a fairly balanced deck overall.

Cards like The Caretaker, Jett Reno, Problem Solver, and Elim Garak, Simple Tailor then interact with the choices you make. When you make a choice, it's called "facing a dilemma," and these cards, along with others, trigger every time you face a dilemma. We can see this is a pretty popular archetype, as it takes the best parts of control and aggro and finds a middle ground that's exciting to build around.

Arguably the most traditional archetype, Klingons rely on all-out aggression, creating and sacrificing token creatures to buff permanents, and swinging wide to earn a win.

Given how well the black-red archetype fits the general Klingon vibe, there's no need to go out of your way to fit the creature type into a different vibe just because the obvious seems too obvious. Theming is important in Universes Beyond sets, so it's nice to see everything work well for a major aspect of the Star Trek set here with the Klingons.

We expect this to be a very popular pick for prerelease and beyond, as drafting to win early is so often an easy path to victory against any deck that needs time to build, especially if someone has gone for more than two colors.

Another hugely popular draft pick will be red-green Landfall. This mechanic has returned in quite a few sets, but is very prevalent in Star Trek. While only ten cards sport the mechanic, they're extremely easy to build around. The remainder of your red-green deck should be ramp and big, powerful creatures.

Red-green is often a slower but higher-power version of black-red, so there can be some crossover between the two. Be wary of branching out into a tri-color deck, though, as you may spread your cards and strategy too thin.

The Star Trek set offers plenty of ways to gain life and start dishing out +1/+1 counters. This makes green-white one of the standout draft archetypes in the set, but it also creates too much choice and forces you to build a focused deck around mechanics you may already have too many of once you've finished picking your cards.

You'll want to focus on creatures that buff your ability to dish out counters, like The Doctor, EMH, which gives a target creature a +1/+1 counter when it enters, then gives a +1/+1 to each creature you control that already has a counter on it. Proliferation isn't available, but that doesn't mean there aren't ways to kinda do it without the exact mechanic being present.

Another artifact-heavy archetype, white-black is usually about life gain and sacrificing, but in Star Trek, it's all about the Borg. These artifact creatures use the Assimilate mechanic to steal opponents' creatures and put them on your battlefield, only with a +1/+1 counter on them, and stripped of all creature types except for Borg artifact.

We Are The Borg is an early fan favorite Commander precon from this set, and if you get the chance to build around the Borg in a draft, we recommend you take it and coast to victory... yes, it's that good.

Red-blue decks are more than familiar with the concept of stacking noncreature spells alongside a few specific creatures (Izzet Prowess, anyone?) and the Star Trek version of that archetype just replaces Prowess with Scientists.

You'll draw and discard cards to find your big hitters, counter your opponent's big plays, bounce creatures off the board, generate token creatures, and deal damage straight to your opponent's face. Everything we've come to expect from red-blue spell decks. This archetype will be popular simply because it's dominated Standard for years, but that comfort level doesn't make it an instant win in draft conditions.

Not all cards are done when they hit your graveyard, and black-green in Star Trek is all too familiar with this idea. You'll either let cards hit the graveyard from the battlefield, or find ways to get them there from your hand or library, because some cards can be cast directly from there or brought back stronger via another spell or ability.

This isn't new for black-green decks, but watch for the specific ability that supports this archetype: Threshold. This ability kicks in when you have seven or more cards in your graveyard.

One of the mechanics that we're not a fan of is power counting in the red-white archetype. This mechanic requires you to have eight or greater power on the battlefield to trigger creature abilities or upgrades. Our main issue is that it isn't well supported in the set, so building an entire archetype around it feels restrictive.

We don't see this being a hugely common build unless someone simply has no other meaningful options in the cards they draft.

Last, but certainly not least, is green-blue Strange New Worlds. Another archetype built around a new mechanic that also features heavily in a Commander precon: Landing Party. This mechanic gives you access to upgrades and benefits based on the number of differently named lands on the battlefield.

In a Commander deck, this is ideal, but in draft, it puts a lot of pressure on you to snap up every special land type you see to keep your triggers meaningful.

This strikes us as the hardest archetype to build successfully, especially given the nature of drafting, but if you can build a competent deck around it, we imagine it will be immensely fun to play.

#4202. Zenless Zone Zero Version 2.7 brings Angels of Delusion to the battlefield with playable Nangong Yu

Champions Never Fall to the Past indeed, as Zenless Zone Zero prepares for a major update that fans of Angels of Delusion will appreciate.

HoYoverse has delivered another Special Program for the second day running, this time for Zenless Zone Zero. The developer revealed the full details of Version 2.7, subtitled Champions Never Fall to the Past.

This next major update arrives March 24, adding two new Agents, and introducing the Hollow Champion competition.

Most things in Version 2.7 follow on from the Hollow Champion competition, which brings together old friends and familiar faces, as well interesting newcomers. Everyone is in it to win some big rewards and earn glory.

Among the unexpected participants the competition has attracted are the Public Security's Metropolitan Order Division, and even some former Calydon's Sweepers. A big challenge that awaits is Black Wolf Romeul, who’s capable of increasing his Crit Damage Resistance and Interruption Resistance by activating a Corruptive Barrier.

Romeul can also cause enemies to continuously lose HP, but you can beat him by putting together a squad that can deal sustained Anomaly damage, which will break through the barrier quickly.

Our first new arrival in Version 2.7 is Cissia of the Metropolitan Order Division. She is an S-Rank Electric Attack Agent who automatically gains three stacks of Venom when she enters the battle. Each stack deals Electric Damage while also increasing her Crit Rate for a time.

When she runs out of Venom, which will happen, Cissia can generate more stacks by using her EX Special Attack. She can also use her Basic Attack, Serpent's Kiss, to better utilise the new stacks of Venom she generates.

The other new Agent may be the more exciting. Nangong Yu, the captain and lead dancer of the Angels of Delusion, can now be part of your team. Nangong Yu is an S-Rank Ether Stun Agent who can boost her team’s Anomaly Buildup Rate against Stunned enemies.

Being part of an idol group has its perks, because she automatically regenerates Downbeat as time goes on, and even more any time a squad member inflicts an enemy with Anomaly. Nangong Yu can then use Downbeat - after enough has been accumulated - on charged attacks that keep enemies stunned for longer. Her Ultimate triggers Ether Veil: Delusion Reprise, which boosts the entire squad’s Attack.

Returning Agents in Version 2.7 will be Yidhari, the S-Rank Ice Rupture Agent, as well as Seed, the Electric Attack Agent.

Outside of all the very important action in the core story, this chapter also brings new themed events to Lumina Square’s Simmer Hot Pot Restaurant. The Simulated Battle Trial is also getting some love, with updated mechanics and new enemy line-ups.

Catch up on our recently updated Zenless Zone Zero character tier list, and don’t forget to check out these Zenless Zone Zero codes before you jump in for some free stuff.

#4201. Crimson Desert Enhanced Adds Surprise Free Trial For All Xbox Series X|S Owners

Ever wanted to play Crimson Desert on your Xbox Series X or Xbox Series S without buying it? You're in luck! It's been announced this week that Crimson Desert Enhanced has received a five-hour free trial on the Xbox Store.

There are no catches with this as far as we're aware - simply search for the game on your Xbox console (specifically "Crimson Desert Enhanced" and not any other version), and you should see a prompt to download the free trial.

This will remain available to download until January 7th, so you've got a couple of months to take advantage.

If you end up really liking it, the good news is that your progress will transfer over to the main game should you choose to purchase it, although keep in mind that the trial can't be restarted over and over again.

All of this is in celebration of the new Charting the Unknown DLC, the trailer for which we'll leave at the bottom of this article. It's an absolutely massive expansion that adds a ton of content on top of the base game, and it's available for £19.99 / $24.99 on the Xbox Store as of yesterday.

As for why Crimson Desert is now called "Crimson Desert Enhanced", it's because they've added "new cutscenes and story moments, plus expanded voice-over and language support" alongside all the updates that have arrived since launch, so now is technically the best time ever to give it a go. Let us know what you think of the free trial!

#4200. Here's The Best Graphics And Performance Mode For Phantom Blade Zero On PlayStation 5

Phantom Blade Zero is out now for everyone as a console exclusive on PlayStation 5 and on PC via Steam and the Epic Games Store as well. If you missed it, it's my favorite action game of the year so far, and you can read why in Game Informer's Phantom Blade Zero review. That explains why I think you should check the game out; Game Informer's list of Phantom Blade Zero tips and tricks will get you some key information I wish I had when I started the game; and this guide I wrote up about the requirements you need to get the best ending in Phantom Blade Zero will help you find all story-critical content in the game.

However, you're looking for advice on which of the three visual modes Phantom Blade Zero offers you should use on your PS5. This here piece is for you.

Phantom Blade Zero has three visual modes on PS5 Pro: Quality, Balanced, and Performance. I tested all three. My personal favorite was Balanced, which gives you an upscaled (checkerboarded) 4K resolution at 40 FPS, as long as you have a 120Hz TV with VRR. If you have a 120Hz TV, it likely has VRR because most major manufacturers include it with 120Hz. I like this mode because the upscaled 4K looks beautiful, just a hair less than native 4K, and if you aren't someone super trained on those details, I'd wager you won't notice the difference. The best part is that this mode offers 40 FPS gameplay, which, contrary to how math works, is halfway between 30 FPS and 60 FPS; I'm not kidding, look it up. As such, 40 FPS feels much smoother than 30 FPS, and you're still getting crisp 4K resolution. It's a win-win for me and my go-to mode when a game offers it. That said, if you don’t have a PS5 Pro, you won’t see this Balanced mode.

The Performance mode offers an upscaled 2K resolution with a pretty locked 60 FPS. Phantom Blade Zero is an extremely fast, fluid action game, so I think many people will want the buttery smoothness of 60 FPS gameplay. If that's you, pick the Performance mode. Sure, its resolution is lower, and it will look blurrier and less crisp than the other two modes, but if you aren't switching back and forth often or looking at side-by-side images, you likely won't notice.

Quality mode is native 4K resolution (absolutely beautiful, the best visual image you can get playing Phantom Blade Zero), but at 30 FPS... and for a game like this, I don't think 30 FPS does it justice. I don't really recommend this mode for combat, but if you're just waltzing around Wulin, grabbing screenshots and such, turn it on and bask in the wonders of developer S-Game's art team. Note: There is an option for ray tracing on PS5 Pro. I tested all three graphics modes with it on and off and noticed zero performance changes or issues. So, use ray tracing – it’s nice!

And, in case you missed it, below is an image of the PC system requirements and specs needed to play Phantom Blade Zero on Steam and the Epic Games Store:

In the meantime, read Game Informer's Phantom Blade Zero review, then check out our list of Phantom Blade Zero tips and tricks we wish we knew before starting the game. Then check out our breakdown of the requirements to see the best ending in the game.

#4198. Heartopia goes to the movies with its next event

Heartopia's Whale Island will soon host a new event that's all about the magic of cinema.

Heartopia’s next in-game event has been announced, and it’s one you may not have seen coming. Developer XD Games revealed Dreamlight Cinematics Festival, an upcoming limited-time event that celebrates cinema and movie-making.

Dreamlight Cinematics kicks off March 21, and will run through May 1, available across the game’s PC and mobile versions.

Dreamlight Cinematics Festival takes place on Whale Island. And, perhaps as an unofficial Oscars tie-in, it’s all about classic Hollywood filmmaking. Not only that, it also celebrates the aesthetics and industrial design of that era.

All around the game’s world, you’ll be able to find festival-themed collectables, which you can then use to unlock free Time-Limited Exhibition Passes.

If you log in during the event’s runtime, you’ll get the Car Cinema furniture set for free. This cosmetic bundle comes with chairs that are modelled after vintage vehicles, as well as poster display stands with unique movie making-themed decorations.

If you’re looking to spend some money, the Deluxe Festival Pack comes with a large Island Sunset Billboard, which you can place outside your home so everyone knows you spent that money. The same pack also comes with the Popcorn Movie Ticket chat bubble skin, and a 10% bonus to Festival Tokens when you sell stuff at the store.

Regardless of which pack you get, you’ll earn collection points for each, which puts you on the path to unlocking outfits like the Dreamlight Cinematics Festival-specific Modern Show Dandy and Modern Show Belle. There’s also a Cinematic Moments building material set launching with this event.

For now, we have the above reveal trailer to go on, which does offer some idea of what it’s going to look like in-game. Until things kick off on the weekend, you best arm yourself with some Heartopia codes.

#4196. Pokemon TCG Delta Reign: Hands-On Preview

Sam Woods is TheGamer’s Senior Reporter. He’s been in games journalism since 2020 and has undertaken a variety of roles in that time. These have included roles such as SEO Editor, Managing Editor at DualShockers, and Global Head of Gaming, and he's also been seen on the BBC. He was promoted to the Senior Reporter position in 2025 following a series of high-quality reports and exclusives for TheGamer.

Since 2020, Sam has written over 3,000 articles and specializes in telling the stories of the people behind the games. He’s interviewed the biggest game directors, some of the industry’s top talents, told the stories of how indie games came to be, and spoken to players about what really makes them tick. He’s also interviewed some of the world’s biggest musical artists to find out how the medium has inspired their work, and TV and Film actors about their roles in video game adaptations. He even hosted a PAX panel in 2021 and made a documentary in 2024 surrounding the creation of a Disney game.

Alongside this, Sam focuses on breaking news. He got the scoop on Perfect Dark’s cancellation, provided context on some AI drama, and revealed that Lady Dimitrescu’s actress would love to step back into the character’s giant shoes. These articles have been picked up by the biggest gaming sites, including IGN, GameSpot, and PC Gamer. He also loves to dive into the numbers behind the games.

Sam’s journey in games journalism has taken him all over the world. He’s covered Gamescom in Germany, Summer Game Fest in Los Angeles, and Tokyo Game Show in Japan, each on three occasions.

He’s been learning Japanese since 2024 with the intention of identifying and translating Japanese-language news and bringing it to English-language audiences first, something he’s done countless times.

Sam’s first review was 2020’s Battletoads reboot, and he’s since reviewed games in The Legend of Zelda, Super Mario, and Pokemon franchises.

The Pokemon Trading Card Game is riding a real wave at the moment. If you set the scalping and stock issues aside, the 30th Anniversary Expansion is one of the best in a long time. It celebrates the TCG's history, with work from artists new and old and returning cards from some of the game’s most notable eras. Any set that followed would struggle, then: How do you match peak?

Unfortunately, Delta Reign had that unenviable task, and despite one of the coolest Rayquaza cards in history, after going hands-on with it ahead of launch, it fails to even come close to matching the expansion that came before it.

Like many recent sets, Delta Reign is a small one. With 141 cards, it sits well below many of Scarlet and Violet’s main sets in terms of size, but after years of begging for smaller expansions, I’ve realized that may not always be a good thing.

Sure, smaller expansions mean less filler cards and ultimately, less bulk, but there is far less variety overall. Delta Reign has six SIRs: Two trainers, two that look like full art cards (Mega Golurk and Mega Golisopod), and two bangers (Raikou and Rayquaza). This seems fairly standard for the more recent sets, but it's almost half the amount from Destined Rivals, the last ScVi expansion.

Sure, it’s great news for Master Set collectors, but not so much for those who just want to collect pretty cards.

Thankfully, Delta Reign has one saving grace outside the very small chance of pulling Rayquaza: its IR selection is great—far better than Chaos Rising and Pitch Black. Of course, there are some misses with Pokemon like Pincurchin and Enamorus, but there are a lot of good ones.

The Eevee, Growlithe, Sprigatito, and Zorua cards are very cute; the Groudon, Magmortar, and Electivire are great, and it's nice to see some random Pokemon like Azurill get a bit of love.

My pulls from my Delta Reign packs were certainly pulls. From 49 packs, I managed four full arts, five IRs, and an SIR. That’s not a bad haul; it just exemplifies my belief that the variety is not there in recent expansions (30th Anniversary and Ascended Heroes aside).

I was delighted to get my hands on both the Eevee and Growlithe IR, but everything else I pulled ranged from whelming to underwhelming.

The Mega Malamar full art is one of seven featuring pretty undesirable Pokemon, and the three trainers I got were fine. It just so happens that of the SIRs, I managed to pull the worst one in the set: Mega Golisopod ex.

It’s a Pokemon that I have no affinity for, and the card itself looks like nothing more than a full art. I’m a big fan of SIRs that depict scenes, or at least have something going on. This just features the Pokemon in the same pose as its full art card, flipped, with slightly more color.

I can’t really complain since the cards came courtesy of The Pokemon Company for review. However, if I’d spent ~$300+ to pull this, I’d be pretty disappointed.

I’m aware that comparing Delta Reign to the 30th Anniversary Expansion is a little unfair. One is a holiday set with tons to love, while the other is a standard expansion. Even compared to other standard expansions, though, this new one falls a little flat.

I felt similarly about Perfect Order, Chaos Rising, and Pitch Black. It feels like the TCG is in a little bit of a rut. Its popularity certainly isn’t waning, but from a personal perspective, I feel like some of the spark is missing—especially so here.

It has a range of great IRs, but the SIRs generally let the set down. I’d like The Pokemon Company to find a better middle ground between whopping expansions and those that are too small to have a good mix of cards.

#4195. Kojima's Xbox-Published OD KNOCK Gets A New Game Poster

Keeping up with Kojima and what he's working on is always a fun task, as we never really know what he's up to, how far along it is, when we'll hear from him again, and all that jazz.

Hideo Kojima's OD KNOCK was announced at The Game Awards in 2023, and yet we know hardly anything about the game. Last night, Kojima returned to provide us with another bump of his Xbox published OD, with a brand-new game poster.

It depicts Sophia Lillis' character looking up towards a windy red object. It kind of looks like a red broomstick, but honestly? Who knows what it is. Her character doesn't appear to be screamin' good and proper like in the previous poster, but they do share the same message: "For all players and screamers".

Sure, it's a pretty basic poster all things considered, but do you know what? It's something! Lord knows all we want is to know more about OD KNOCK and when we'll be able to understand what makes it so scary.

Earlier in the year, worries that Kojima's Xbox-published game was getting canned started to circulate, but those concerns have since been put to rest by Xbox boss Asha Sharma, who declared "to invention and adventure together with Xbox" when she visited Kojima Productions in September.

We have no idea when OD KNOCK will hit Xbox consoles, but what we do know is that when it does eventually release, we'll be here at Pure Xbox to bring you all the coverage.

#4194. The Duskbloods Delayed To 2027 So FromSoftware Can Adjust 'Game Rules And Balancing'

While the 2025 reveal of the Switch 2 came with many surprises, none were as unexpected as The Duskbloods. It's a Switch 2 exclusive, multiplayer-only title from FromSoftware, the developer behind games like Dark Souls and Elden Ring; in other words, not your typical Nintendo game. While The Duskbloods was originally scheduled to launch sometime this year, today the developer announced it's pushing the game's launch to 2027.

According to a post on The Duskbloods' X account, the main reason for the delay was balance-related. Here's the full statement:

While development of "The Duskbloods" is at the final adjustment stage, we have made the decision to move the launch window to 2027. We apologize to players who have been kindly awaiting the release of this title and thank you for your patience and support. During the network test, we saw active interest in the core concepts of the game, including combat, strategic depth, and player expression. To further enhance these aspects, we have decided to move the launch, allowing time for final adjustments to game rules and balancing.

We attended a hands-on preview session earlier this year and came away very positive, and sentiment was similar following the game's closed network test (that is, when the servers were working properly). It's not surprising that the devs have changes in mind following so much public feedback, though it is a little surprising that it will take until sometime next year for those adjustments to be complete.

To tide you over until the game's launch, check out our in-depth preview impressions or watch the video above to hear our live commentary over gameplay footage. You can also hear us discuss the game on our podcast, The Game Informer Show.

#4193. All the hype has already made Crimson Desert one of the biggest launches on Steam this year

We're merely days away from the end of the first quarter of 2026, and Crimson Desert has come in clutch to join the list of big sellers.

Crimson Desert, the open-world action RPG off-shoot from Korean MMO Black Desert Online, has officially launched, nearly six years after it was initially revealed. The game has been building up a lot of momentum over the years, which recently coalesced to turn it into one of 2026’s most anticipated titles.

All of it has been leading up to this moment, and the game appears to have landed smoothly, though not without controversy, as has seemingly become part of its MO.

It has not been 24 hours since Crimson Desert launched on PC and consoles, and it’s already become a big hit. On Steam, one of two stores where the game can be purchased (the other being the Epic Games Store), the game shot to the top of the charts.

The action RPG continued to accumulate more and more players on Steam, peaking at a very respectable 239,045 concurrent players (via SteamDB). Though its success was very much expected, we perhaps didn’t predict its peak would be that high.

Indeed, Crimson Desert has been in Steam’s top 100 global sellers list for six weeks, jumping up six spots to become the number one seller this week just before it launched. As we get closer to the weekend, the numbers could climb even higher.

This peak concurrent puts Crimson Desert in the same league as several of the other major releases of the first quarter of 2026. The top spot continues to belong to Slay the Spire 2, which peaked at a staggering 574,638 concurrent players. It happened just days after the juggernaut Resident Evil Requiem achieved its own 344,214 peak concurrent, which was the year’s highest up until Slay the Spire 2’s release. All three are well ahead of Nioh 3’s 88,045 peak concurrent, and Marathon’s nearly identical peak of 88,337.

Crimson Desert has seen something of a mixed reception by critics. James gave it three stars in our review, saying it “lacks the connective sinew to be truly functional,” which is a common criticism shared by other outlets. Many also lamented the sheer number of systems fighting for player attention, its poorly explained mechanics, and counterintuitive controls.

On Steam, at least, players have similarly been divided, with the current Steam user rating sitting at Mixed, based on 8,728 reviews. Unsurprisingly, most of the negative reactions fall on the clunky controls and the game’s tendency to, as one Steam user put it, “so miserably tries to be everything at once, and fails to be anything at all.”

#4191. Crimson Desert's first patch aims at fixing controls, but it mostly affects mouse and keyboard

The first post-launch patch for Crimson Desert is here, and the list of changes is promising, even if it doesn't go far enough to address some deeper issues.

Crimson Desert has been out for a few days now, and as positive as its been received by many players, the game suffers from several fundamental issues that anyone who’s played it has called out.

Perhaps the loudest one of those has been how the game controls, which is a problem that stems from the complexity of controls themselves, as well as the underlying animations behind many of the actions the player character performs.

In the first case, at least, something is being done.

Developer Pearl Abyss rolled out patch 1.00.03 for Crimson Desert on Monday. The patch is available now on Steam and PlayStation, with Xbox and the Epic Games Store following “at a later time.”

Today’s update follows a letter to players the developer issued on Saturday. The letter generally acknowledged player feedback, but specifically pointed to complaints about the game’s clunky controls as something of a focus for the team.

The action RPG has actually broken its launch peak concurrent player numbers over the weekend, though only by a few thousands more. Its Steam user review rating has also improved over the same period.

This latest update only includes an initial set of fixes, but Pearl Abyss vowed to keep working on addressing all other points of feedback. A highlight in 1.00.03 is the addition of a Storage at Howling Hill Camp, which can be used to store inventory items.

The most important changes, of course, affect how the game controls on keyboard and mouse. Pearl Abyss included several fixes and altered some of the default presets to make the experience less painful when playing the game with a keyboard and mouse.

There are sadly no changes to controllers, but it is something that the developer said we can expect to see in future patches. More improvements for keyboard and mouse setups are in the works, too.

Beyond the control changes, patch 1.00.03 also includes a set of gameplay tweaks, especially when it comes to enemy health and difficulty. It also makes fast travelling more convenient, and brings a few fixes to NPC dialogue. You can read the full change log on Steam.

If you’re deep in Crimson Desert already, we definitely recommend giving our guides a look. We recently added new pages to help you figure out where to socket your Abyss Gear, how to find Contribution Points - and where to spend them, as well as more generally helpful information like how to expand your inventory, and how to reveal the map.

#4190. Assassin’s Creed Franchise Update Reveals Codename Hexe News Coming Next Year, New Game Plus for Valhalla, And Confirms No New Remakes

Ubisoft has released a fall update on the Assassin’s Creed franchise, providing news big and small on its flagship series. The news includes updates for existing games and smaller but significant insights on the various upcoming Assassin’s Creed games previously announced.

In terms of current games, Assassin’s Creed Valhalla is getting a long-requested New Game Plus thanks to a new update coming on November 5. This means you can start a fresh game while bringing over your progression items/level from your previous playthrough. This update will also introduce the following features:

This news comes a few days after New Game Plus arrived in Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced.

Codname Invictis, a PvP multiplayer game, remains in development as Ubisoft shares it has incorporated feedback from players who, according to Ubisoft, “saw great potential in the foundations but wanted more of the pillars that define Assassin's Creed.” To this end, Ubisoft has spent months reworking Invictis to reflect this vague feedback and say the game is “now evolving in an exciting direction that better reflects those pillars while staying true to its multiplayer ambitions.”

As for the next single-player Assassin’s Creed, Codename Hexe, Ubisoft says it will share the next major update on this game in 2027. First announced in 2022, Codename Hexe is set during the 17th-century reign of the Holy Roman Empire, and the era's witch hunts will play a significant role.

With the release of Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced earlier this year, Ubisoft has given fans what they'll likely see as a disappointing update on potential future remakes: “One thing we want to be transparent about today is that we currently have no other Assassin's Creed remake actively in development. Our teams are already focused on the next chapter of Assassin's Creed titles, including projects you haven't heard about yet, featuring new settings and stories.”

However, Ubisoft adds that this door isn’t closed for good. “Like many of you, we love the idea of revisiting our classic titles, and we'll keep exploring opportunities to bring older titles back,” says Ubisoft.

Ubisoft’s next update concerns the live-action Assassin's Creed series in production for Netflix. They say the show is “nearing completion” in Rome and that award-winning composer Hannah Peel (Insomnia, Rogue Agent, Game of Thrones: The Last Watch) is composing the score.

Lastly, Ubisoft teases big celebrations are planned for 2027, which marks the 20th anniversary of the Assassin's Creed franchise. It's keeping details to itself for now, but states it's "preparing a year of reveals, updates, rewards, and community moments. "

For more on Assassin's Creed, check out our review of Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced.

#4189. MTG: Top 6 Commander Deckbuilding Tools

Building a Magic: The Gathering Commander deck is a fun, albeit long process thanks to the more than 33,000 cards legal in the format. This is where online deckbuilding tools become priceless, because some of the best tools will take your existing decklist and suggest changes based on what you're trying to achieve.

We've collated a list of six tools you should check out if you're preparing to build or adjust any of your Commander decks. Whether you're focusing on power level, price, or strategies, each of these tools will help you become a better deckbuilder, but don't ask them to help with missing your triggers.

Updated on November 2, 2026 by Niall Walsh: We revisited this list after a long time to refresh it and add a relatively new tool to the list in EDHTuner.

One of the newer tools on the market is EDHTuner, which takes your existing deck (you can import it from other deckbuilding tools) and gives you valuable insights on which cards to remove and which to add, based on the strategies it detects in the current build.

This AI-free tool also runs thousands of test games with each deck and each individual card replacement, so you can see how even small changes can affect a deck's performance.

If you're worried about brackets, you can also see which bracket your deck falls into, and it can suggest ways to increase your deck's power level if you want to be more competitive or decrease it if you're looking to be fairer during casual games.

Free, simple, and quick, EDHTuner has everything you need from a Commander deckbuilding tool, and as its feature set is built out and it potentially becomes less reliant on importing decks built in other tools, it could very well shoot up this list.

We're running through the best preconstructed MTG Commander decks for new players to use while they get used to the format and Magic in general.

Commander Spellbook is "the search engine for EDH combos" and is a fantastic way to search for powerful combos. From the homepage, you can enter a card and find any combos that use it, or use advanced search to find combos by a specific outcome, your Commander's color identity, or even how many cards you need to pull it off.

Commander Spellbook is great because it helps you tune your Commander deck to your playgroup's power level. You can use it to find combos to include, but you can also use it to pin down any accidental combos you didn't intend. There's nothing worse than somebody comboing off at a low-power game, especially when even that player didn't realize it could happen beforehand.

One quirk of the Commander format is that it's easy to use cards that do almost the same thing as another card, just slightly worse. For example, a Cancel and a Counterspell do the same thing, but Counterspell costs one generic mana less. That's what StrictlyBetter works out for you.

The best time to use StrictlyBetter is after you've finished a rough draft of your deck and want to add a few finishing touches. Copy the decklist into the site, and it will scan its community-driven directories to see if any of your cards could be replaced with something better. The community votes on each suggestion, so you can easily see cards some people think are better but might not be the best alternative.

Of course, Commander as a format is all about player expression. Don't feel as though you must be running the best possible card in every situation – Underground Sea may be better than a Sunken Hollow, but is also vastly more expensive, and maybe it's a step too far for your deck's power level. StrictlyBetter is just a good way to find easy improvements when you're struggling to know where to go next.

There are lots of deckbuilding sites out there, like TappedOut, Archidekt, and MTGGoldfish, but Moxfield is by far the easiest and most powerful one of the lot.

As a deckbuilding site, Moxfield's main goal is to help you organize and track your deck, draft new ones, or share them with other people. Through it, you can set the format you're building for, and it can help you avoid accidentally adding illegal cards. It can count your mana costs to help you get the right number of lands, track your mana curve to avoid unfortunate spikes in mana costs, and even look through other users' submissions for suggestions.

One of the best things about Moxfield is how many ways you can organize your cards in the deck view. While you can stick with the default card type listing, you can group and sort your deck in loads of different ways, like mana cost, color, rarity, the set it debuted in, and even custom tags. It's so easy to tag cards as things like "ramp", "draw", or "removal" to ensure you're hitting everything a deck needs to be able to do.

More than just a deckbuilder, though, Moxfield has lots of resources that help you test or improve your deck. It has full integration with EDHRec (more on that later), and even has a 'goldfishing' feature that helps you playtest your deck.

EDHRec is the number one database for the Commander format, collating thousands of decklists together to make a resource that can help you build almost any deck possible.

EDHRec ranks Commanders by popularity, which helps you see where the meta is, and it also shows which cards are most commonly played in that Commander's decks. For example, say you want to build a deck for Kwain, Itinerant Meddler. You can search for Kwain, and then scroll down to see all the top cards used in decks that run it as a Commander, like Dictate of Kruphix, Teferi's Ageless Insight, Kami of the Crescent Moon, and Laboratory Maniac.

Each type of card is also individually listed, so if you're looking for lands to put in a Kwain deck, you can scroll to the lands section on EDHRec and see that Prairie Stream, Hallowed Fountain, Glacial Fortress, and Command Tower are the most popular.

Alternatively, it can also sort by the themes of the deck you want to build, instead of a specific Commander. If you know you want to build a Planeswalker-heavy "Superfriends" deck, going to the Planeswalkers theme page shows you that Atraxa, Praetor's Voice, Carth the Lion, Esika God of the Tree, and Sisay, Weatherlight Captain are the most popular Commanders for it, while cards like Oath of Teferi and Nicol Bolas, Dragon-God are the most popular cards in the 99.

EDHRec is a huge resource that can help take the decision anxiety out of making a deck. Whether you're looking for those last cards to add, or want inspiration for your next deck, it's one of the best community resources the Magic community has ever built.

There are a lot of cards to sort through when building a deck. Though you could look through Gatherer, the official Magic database, Scryfall is a much more powerful alternative that's simultaneously a lot easier to use.

From the homepage, you can search through the names of any card ever published. For example, typing "Dig" can show you Dig Through Time, Gravedigger, Harmonic Prodigy, Dig Up, and more. This is great for finding a specific card you want to check; it also shows official rulings, images of most prints, what sets it's legal in, and even secondary market prices. But individual cards are just the tip of the iceberg of what Scryfall can do.

The advanced search is incredible, and through it, you can search through every card's rule text, flavor text, color identity, look up full set galleries, find specific artists, and even find which cards mention your favorite characters. There are loads of unofficial categories to look through as well, such as whether a card's double-sided, has an etched foil version, has hybrid mana, or virtually anything else you could want to look for.

For most deckbuilding, the most important things to search by are the text field, which searches the main rules box on every card, colors to find the right color cards for your deck, and the type line to weed out creatures from sorceries, or look for the exact creature type you want.

Scryfall is an absolute powerhouse of a tool. It might take a little while to get to grips with its quirks and syntax, but once you have, finding exactly what you need for any deck is a breeze.

#4188. Sir Patrick Stewart, Star Trek, X-Men, And Myriad Video Games Actor, Passes Away

According to a report from The Hollywood Reporter, actor Sir Patrick Stewart has passed away at the age of 86. Stewart spokesperson, Kelly Bush Novak, shared that he died after “a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia.”

Stewart was best known for his roles as Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation (and its various spinoffs) and Charles Xavier in the X-Men films, but he did plenty of video game performing, too. Stewart played Emperor Uriel Septim VII in The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion, one of the first characters you meet in the game, and Zobek in Castlevania: Lords of Shadow. He also played Jean-Luc Picard in about 10 different Star Trek games and Charles Xavier in five different X-Men games.

Stewart will always be a crucial voice and face in the legacy of sci-fi entertainment. Jean-Luc Picard will undoubtedly be an enduring and important character in the Star Trek franchise, and that's thanks to Stewart's portrayal of the starship captain. His portrayal of Charles Xavier also helped to legitimize the comic book movie, and he will appear again as the character in this year's upcoming Avengers: Doomsday.

Our thoughts are with his friends and family, and the millions of fans (of which I include myself) who are mourning his loss. Let's all drink some Earl Grey tea in his honor today.
