#4142. Zenless Zone Zero Version 2.8 is refreshing your team comps with a new mechanic, and the game is coming to Steam

Zenless Zone Zero will soon become the first HoYoverse game to make its way to Steam, though we wish we had more details.

HoYoverse just wrapped up a pretty exciting Zenless Zone Zero Special Program that not only delivered all the details on the next big update, it also came with the unexpected announcement that the action RPG is on its way to Steam.

Previously, all HoYoverse games with PC versions have always been directly available from the developer’s website, or through the Epic Games Store. In other words, Zenless Zone Zero will soon mark the massive company’s debut on Valve’s platform.

The main focus of the livestream, of course, has been Version 2.8, otherwise known as New Eridan Sunset. This upcoming release is scheduled for May 6, though the Steam version does not yet have a date.The new release sees the release of two new Agents, as well as the brand-new Wind attribute enemy.

The release also acts as the last chapter of Season 2, and it sees Ramiel becoming the main target of different factions in the Outer Ring. The two new arrivals, together with Proxies and Cissia will embark on a quest to learn the new identity of Ramiel.

The first new Agent is Promeia, the executioner of Krampus. She’s an S-Rank Ice Anomaly Agent who can consume Trial by Cold to trigger Abloom on enemies. This is done by converting Corrosive Chill.

By using her EX Special Attack, she can enter the Bound Absolution state, which allows her to automatically Perfect Dodge any attack that targets her. If you have another Anomaly or Support Agent on the team, Promeia can further boost the entire squad’s Abloom damage.

The second addition in 2.8 is Starlight - Billy, also an S-Rank Agent, though wielding Physical Rupture instead. This is the upgraded form of Billy, and he arrives on a combat motorcycle to bring his signature Starlight Knight to the fight. Through it, he can deliver big Physical burst damage.

The higher Billy’s health, the more Sheer damage he deals. In fact, all Physical damage he deals lands as Sheer damage. Further building on his tank-like role, his skills can also restore his own health.

Re-runs in Version 2.8 will be Lucia in the first half, and Orphie & Magus in the second. The other exciting addition coming with this update is the new Wind attribute enemy, and the accompanying Vortex mechanic.

When an enemy is inflicted with the Wind Attribute Anomaly, any other Anomaly attack type that gets applied will trigger Vortex, rather than Disorder. This deals AoE Anomaly damage of the type that matches the corresponding element.

Throughout the version’s runtime, you’ll be able to take part in the Marcel Bootopia-themed event, which gives you control of Eous and lets you explore a Bangboo resort island. The island has been closed due to an outbreak of Hollows, and you must rescue Bangboos and find treasures.

If you do, you’ll earn Booltergeist and its Bangboo core for your troubles. This is an A-Rank Bangboo that can float around and fire lasers in combat. Its damage is further boosted whenever certain teammates are present.

The Ultimate Verdict Trial is another event you can check out that lets you fight alongside newcomer Promeia, or take part in other mini-activities that all reward Polychrome. Finally, you can look forward to a new Hoshimi Miyabi outfit: Dignified Blossom, which will be available in the store.

Before you jump back in next month, it always helps to catch up on the latest Zenless Zone Zero codes to make sure you’re not missing out on any freebies.

#4141. Three Xbox Games Are Shutting Down Their Servers In November & December 2026

A few notable delistings on the way as well

November has officially arrived, and therefore we thought we'd bring you our latest roundup of games getting delisted over the next few weeks, with this roundup specifically focusing on November and December 2026.

The good news is that there's not much to talk about! Call of Duty: Warzone is undoubtedly the most notable of the bunch here, which has been set to go offline on Xbox One and PS4 for some time. They originally announced that it would go offline when Modern Warfare 4 Season 1 began, and that's now officially set for November 6th, 2026.

Beyond that, NBA 2K25 is losing its servers at the end of the year, while Synduality: Echo of Ada is turning off its in-game purchases in December ahead of a planned full server closure in May of 2027.

Beyond this, we also wanted to bring your attention to Amazon's New World: Aeternum, which is officially shutting down its servers at the end of January 2027. We'll remind you again nearer the time, but it's worth being aware of it now too!

As for upcoming delistings, both Street Outlaws and Street Outlaws 2 will disappear off the Xbox Store at the end of December 2026, so you'll need to buy them before then if you want the ability to re-download them in the future.

We've seen on many occasions that announcements like these can spring up at the last minute, so we'll keep an eye out and let you know of any big reveals over the next couple of months. For now though, the damage doesn't look too bad!

#4140. Nintendo Shares Ocarina Of Time Switch 2 Design Sketches

The latest Ask the Developer interviews are positively packed with interesting tidbits about the making of Ocarina of Time on Switch 2. One such story is all about the game's reimagined visuals, which Nintendo was even kind enough to share some initial sketches of.

According to Art Director Aya Shida, the team was consciously fighting a battle between making the game more realistic with the improved power of the Switch 2, and retaining the spirit of the original — a somewhat dark world, filled with weird characters. She therefore relied on phrases like “a puppet-show feel” and “the analogue feel of practical effects films” during development to reflect the goal: "both create a convincing sense that the characters truly exist within their respective fantasy worlds".

When it came to these characters, the team wanted to preserve their "familiar presence" first and foremost, before adding "designs unique to this game" on top. Hence, we end up with a recognisable Child Link, but with far more costume bells and whistles attached.

Here's a handful of the design sketches themselves, so you can see how the characters were initially conceptualised:

The same can be said for the game's iconic maps. "We didn't want to change the feel of each location or the way the locations connected with one another," Director HokWai Ng says in the interview, "both of which are so characteristic of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time". The team therefore went back to one of the artists who had worked on illustrations for the N64 original, and asked them to draw a new map for the game.

We even get to see this very sketch, too:

Such an approach resulted in the style we see today, which, we must say, has grown on us over the last few months — it really is quite the looker, eh?

One thing that is already rubbing some people up the wrong way, mind you, is how the game seemingly opts for SMAA over DLSS for its upscaling and anti-aliasing tech. Footage of the game's preloaded intellectual property notice has been doing the rounds on social media, where AMD FSR 1.0 and SMAA are listed under third-party technologies over Nvidia's DLSS. The same approach was taken on Donkey Kong Bananza, we should point out.

Based on everything that we've seen of the game so far, the DLSS departure doesn't seem to have had all that much negative impact on the finished result, but it's still a shame to see even Nintendo's biggest games missing out — particularly after all the DLSS hype in the console's reveal.

Jim came to Nintendo Life in 2022 and, despite his insistence that The Minish Cap is the best Zelda game and his unwavering love for the Star Wars prequels (yes, really), he has continued to write news and features on the site ever since.

Well I have no complaints about DKB and looking at Zelda no complaints there. And I’m using 65” qd-oled that picks up every detail. Using DLSS does use more overheads system wise than FSR 1 SMAA etc. So there was probably a very good reason for this approach.

Always cool when such sketches are shared with the public - even happier that this Ask the Developer has come out (looking forward to reading it fully when I have the time for it)!

@AI-Generation FSR 1 is a very easy to drop in post rendering option, it’s so easy to drop in on the Steam Deck there’s a toggle to enable it for any game in the system menu. With DLSS and FSR 2 onwards the engine needs to provide motion vectors (how any objects through the scene are moving) so that can be taken into account to produce the superior result.

It made sense when Donkey Kong and Mario Kart (plus all the Switch 2 editions/patches except Pokemon Scarlet/Violet) didn’t include DLSS since it’s not trivial to add support for motion vectors for upscaling to something but I’m a bit puzzled as to why over a year later we still are seeing games using FSR 1 published by Nintendo.

Said engines are incompatible with hardware accelerated upscalers like DLSS. They dont produce the vector information DLSS needs in their current state. #4138. Dispatch celebrates its first anniversary with commentary and storyboard modes for every single episode, if you've got the deluxe edition anyway

A rare insight into how the sausage gets made

I'm going to park my feelings of unease at the fact that it's somehow already been a year since Dispatch came out, as developer AdHoc Studio have revealed some pretty neat sounding additions to the game to commemorate its first anniversary. Well, if you have the deluxe edition anyway (sorry, regular edition owners).

There are two new modes that have arrived with this update (which is already out), one being a cast and crew commentary, the other a storyboard mode. "Over 16 hours of commentary across every episode, with two tracks to choose from in the Settings: Cast or Crew," explains a Steam blog post of the commentary mode. "Different choices unlock different commentary, so your playthrough could share new insights every time you play it. You’ll hear from Aaron Paul, Laura Bailey, Travis Willingham, and more of the cast, plus the people who wrote, directed, and designed the game."

Storyboard mode is quite an unusual one, as it allows you to play the entire game "the way it was first drawn." That means that every single one of the game's episodes can be played while looking at its original storyboards and draft renderings, "so you can see how the scenes and characters were designed before a single frame was animated." Obviously this is something that only really works given how cutscene-focused the game is, and not something that'd be easily possible with other kinds of games, but it's a wonderfully rare insight into how games get made. Neat! Outside of the update which is more broadly applicable to you lot, there is also a concert featuring the game's music happening at Avalon Hollywood in LA on December 3rd. Only one night for that one and there's limited tickets, so expect that to sell out fast.

If you're curious what Dispatch is actually like, here's a few words from Edwin on it: "It's been so long since I played a Telltale-style game that all the Telltale quirks feel novel again. Timed dialogue choices and action QTEs. X will remember that. Hashtag 4 Clementine. Created by a team co-founded by former Walking Dead and Wolf Among Us developers, Dispatch brings all of that charming, movie-night energy to bear on a superhero comedy premise you might broadly recognise from The Boys and Invincible, except that it's more laidback and banter-driven than either of those."

#4137. Genshin Impact Luna 7 brings us the first playable Hexenzirkel as things take a turn in Sumeru

Genshin Impact's Luna 7 update will kick off a new Archon Quest chapter, and deliver some interesting new additions to the playable roster.

HoYoverse just wrapped up a new Genshin Impact Special Program, where the developer revealed everything there is to know about the game’s next major update. Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana, or as its friends call it, Luna 7, was unveiled as part of the showcase.

This next update has a lot going for it, and it will be in players’ hands everywhere on May 20.

Luna 7 will take us back to Sumeru for its new Archon Quest, where a new crisis that threatens to plunge the nation into chaos is brewing. Nahida is out of the picture, and someone who looks suspiciously like Il Dottore has emerged.

If you complete this chapter at launch, you’ll earn up to 560 Primogems, as well as Nicole's Ascension Materials. Nicole is the first of three playable characters arriving with this update. Something else you’ll unlock if you finish the chapter quickly is a new Weekly Boss that HoYo says has “unpredictable abilities.”

And if you haven’t played in a while, don’t worry, you can refer to the Guiding Notes feature to catch you up on what’s been going on in the world. This is part of a larger effort from the team to make story progression more seamless, and also includes improved quest autosave prompts.

Nicole Reeyn is highest-profile and most interesting, being the first playable member of the Hexenzirkel. The mage is a 5-Star Pyro Catalyst wielder intended as a support member of the team. She can boost the ATK of all party members, even those not currently on the field. She also generates a shield while doing so.

Her Elemental Burst allows her to summon an Arcane Projection that follows the active character, sending out Coordinated Attacks that match their Elemental Type. Outside of combat, Nicole can help you find treasures by calling upon a Seelie to guide you to them. Quite fitting, as you’ll be exploring in the inside of the Witch's Lodge in Nicole’s Meeting Point in Luna 7, so bring her along.

Lohen, the Vice Captain of the Knights of Favonius' Fifth Company, is the second new character. Also a 5-Star addition, he is instead a Cryo Polearm wielder designed for aggressive combat. His main use is dealing massive Cryo DMG, and he can do that by managing two resources unique to him: Joy, and Will to Win.

Through his Elemental Skill, he can enter the Masterstroke state, allowing him to build up (and consume) Joy to unleash enhanced skills. The more his teammates fight, the more Will to Win he biulds, which can later be used to boost his effectiveness further. For an even more powerful display of force, bring along a Hexerei character when he’s on your team.

Prune is the third and final addition. Prune is a 4-Star Anemo Catalyst wielder, and her kit is inspired by her Witch Hunter aspirations. Using a bell and a hammer, she can deal DMG of several elements at once, and trigger Swirl reactions.

Nicole, and Lohen will debut in Luna 7’s first half, while Prune will follow in the second. The first half will also see a Durin rerun, with Mavuika returning in the second half. You can look forward to a new limited-time event as part of Luna 7, with a focus on Klee's Little Hexenzirkel.

You’ll find a series of mini-games you can play alongside Prune, as well as Qiqi, Yaoyao, and Sayu. If you play, you could earn the Super Awesome Magic Key, an exclusive weapon skin. Miliastra Wonderland is doing its thing, too, with a new sports festival for you to take part in.

One new gameplay addition worth calling attention to is that Manekins can now perform actions in Teyvat. The Kamera, which you can use to capture moments with Manekins, is getting upgraded, too, with new editing tools and assets.

Before you pick the game back up, be sure to check out our recently-updated Genshin Impact codes page for some free stuff you may be missing.

#4136. An internal Mass Effect 5 trailer has reportedly leaked, offering you a glimpse at the sequel you'll never get to play

Yesterday, only a couple of months after EA went private after having been acquired by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, equity firm Silver Lake, and Jared Kushner's Affinity, it was announced that BioWare are being shut down, with development on their next Mass Effect game cancelled. Now, only a day after this was announced, a trailer that was meant for internal use only has been shared, showing off a rough idea of what the game would be like.

The trailer initially came from a Reddit post by a user without much evidence of its legitimacy, but since then IGN have seemingly been able to verify that it's authentic. Worth noting right away is a message shared at the beginning of the trailer: "The following is in-engine footage from our small team. It uses our pre-production assets." It then goes on to show a former sci-fi military man explaining why he left the war life behind for what looks like a James Bond-esque interplanetary one.

While the whole thing is pre-rendered, there is a loose idea of gameplay here, with the usual gun action paired with some fancy telekinetic abilities. At the end of the trailer we even get a name, Mass Effect Universe. No way of knowing if this was just a working title or if this is what would have been revealed whenever the time came to do so. Perhaps the most notable section is the inclusion of an older Liara T'Soni, who helps the protagonist in a bar fight, begging the question of when the game might be set.

Without further leaks, we only really have this trailer and the words of those who were working on it to get any kind of understanding of what it would have been like. BioWare weren't the only ones to be affected by EA's obvious cost-cutting measures either. Devs working on The Sims, Skate and Battlefield also appear to have lost their jobs as part of the 400 staffers that have been laid off. As always, solidarity with all of the concerned workers.

#4135. Robot smashing catharsis game Virtue and a Sledgehammer is out next week, but there's an experimental visual novella prologue you can play right now

Virtue and a Sledgehammer looks like a satisfying game. There is perhaps no more wonderfully chunky and impact frame friendly a weapon than the reliable sledgehammer, and when put into a game with a description like, "Most people resort to therapy. But you chose the brave option. A sledgehammer," then of course I have to give it a look. Unfortunately, I still have to wait a week to check out the full thing. Fortunately, a prologue to the game just dropped for free that offers a tantalising, and quite different, experience.

Where Virtue and a Sledgehammer is something of an action game, Virtue: Prologue (note the lack of sledgehammer) goes all in on just vibes as a visual novel. It's described thusly: "Virtue: Prologue is an experimental visual novella and companion piece to the violent catharsis of Virtue and a Sledgehammer. Navigate the complex feelings of your first love: a hot, rich boy from Barcelona. Sneak into the graveyard at night with your sister, or climb a tree for high-stakes conversations."

First of all, is this the first time someone has used the term "visual novella"? I've certainly seen plenty enough short visual novels, but can't recall any of them being referred to as a visual novella. Please, visual novel writers, take this up if only because I think it's very cute. Second of all, Virtue: Prologue certainly has the juice. I've had a quick glance at it myself and it's a clever use of some of the assets you'll find in the full game, with some striking use of text and a clever way of using your left mouse button.

As a word of warning, you should probably skip this one if you suffer from photosensitive epilepsy. The game is not shy about using flashing images, and as far as I can tell there's no way to reduce that effect, so might be worth coming back to if such a thing is rectified. You'll have to keep an eye on that yourself though, as the game is only available through Pantaloon's Playbill website, which you'll also need to sign up for with your email. Still, a neat little introduction to the game, and something to tide you over for the next few days.

#4134. Mystic Messenger's most loyal players are getting banned in droves for seemingly playing the game too much

With the 10th anniversary of Mystic Messenger nearly upon us, the dating sim has inexplicably begun issuing wide-spread bans for its most active players.

Mystic Messenger, arguably one of the best dating sims around, has been dormant for about seven years. Despite not receiving new content or any meaningful updates in all that time, the game remains popular with its core fans, many of whom just woke up to some shocking news about their accounts.

The free-to-play mobile dating sim has started banning players with seemingly too many Hourglasses - the game’s virtual currency - saved up in their accounts. So far, it looks like players with 1,000 or more have been targeted, but others with far fewer hoards have reported getting the axe, too.

The news exploded on the Mystic Messenger subreddit overnight, with over a dozen reports from players logging in to play normally, only to receive an in-game notice that their accounts had been banned.

The message players received is identical, and doesn’t mention the specific reason for the ban. “Your account has been banned because abusive behavior has been detected from your account,” it reads, ending with a support email address the affected user can contact if they believe they’d banned in error.

It didn’t take a while for players to realise that most, if not all of the bans are for players with thousands of Hourglasses in their accounts. The virtual currency can both be acquired in-game just by playing, as well as through direct real-money purchases.

For a nearly ten-year-old game that stopped receiving content three years into its life, it’s easy to see how a dedicated group of players would be able to acquire so many Hourglasses by simply playing regularly for so long.

When contacted by the affected players, Cheritz, the developer and publisher of the game, has instructed them to send receipts of how they acquired Hourglasses (assuming they were purchased) to verify whether or not they’d been fraudulently obtained.

Considering that Mystic Messenger has practically been abandoned by its developer, certain exploits have emerged over the years that allowed players to farm Hourglasses faster than intended, but those instances have always been dealt with then and there.

The blanket and sudden nature of this ban is what’s spooked players, especially those who’ve been logging in for years and never thought accruing in-game currency from playing the game too much would make them the target of a ban.

The running theory is that most of the bans are unintentional, and may be the result of a new automated security system that’s been implemented. It’s entirely possible, especially if its’s AI-based, that the new system simply couldn’t distinguish between those who have earned (or bought) their Hourglasses fairly, and those who used exploits.

The timing of the ban wave is also suspect. With the game’s 10th anniversary coming up in July, it could be that Cheriz is preparing to release a large update for Mystic Messenger, which may include new content. If most of the playerbase is already sitting on massive amounts of in-game currency, they may simply use that to fast-track their way to unlocking the new content, which would greatly affect the developer’s bottom line.

This is a problem that other live service games have run into in the past. Just recently, extraction shooter Arc Raiders added a cap to the amount of Cred players can hold in their accounts very quickly after its launch. That currency is used to buy cosmetic sets in the store, so the logic is easy to follow.

All of that has certainly put a damper on the enthusiasm of the game’s most active players, many of whom were excited to get together in person for the coming 10th anniversary, participate in community nights and so on to celebrate.

It’s also disheartening to see a fanbase so loyal; playing a game as regularly for so long without new content, to be treated so poorly. Even without knowing what the game is, it’s impressive that so many people have kept the flag of their favourite game flying for so long.

#4133. Poll: Are You Happy with Your PS Plus Essential Games for November 2026?

November's PS Plus Essential games were revealed earlier this week, and I think it's quite an interesting selection.

That's because all three games offer something completely different. We've got a fairly big-name headliner, a collection of remastered adventures, and a highly-rated indie on our hands.

Dead Island 2 is up first. This punchy sequel combines hyper violent zombie-slaying with tongue-in-cheek storytelling across an apocalyptic Los Angeles.

It's a good laugh — especially if you team up with a couple of friends online — and a solid action romp.

Tomb Raider 4-6 Remastered is next on the list, and while Lara Croft's fourth, fifth, and sixth outings are rarely mentioned with the same kind of reverence as her original trilogy, they're still packed with nostalgic platforming goodness.

And last but certainly not least — go and check the review scores — is Monster Train 2. This is a deck-building roguelike full of fantastical creatures, and it's super addictive once you've wrapped your head around the turn-based mechanics.

I get it: some people hear "deck-building" and "roguelike", and they turn away — but there's a reason this hugely expanded sequel is so highly regarded.

News PS Plus Essential Games for November 2026 Announced

So, what do you make of November's PS Plus offering? As always, cast your vote in the polls, and then explain yourself in the comments section below.

#4132. Blizzard Is Getting Our Hopes Up Again For World Of Warcraft On Xbox

One of Xbox's biggest releases of 2026 isn't actually releasing on Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S - it's Blizzard's World of Warcraft: Forever, which is still a PC exclusive launching on November 5th.

That said, we've seen signs that Blizzard might be pushing towards a native Xbox release in the future, as they've implemented native controller support for WoW: Forever meaning it'll be playable on devices like the ROG Xbox Ally.

And, in a recent interview with GamesRadar, World of Warcraft Vice President Holly Longdale appeared to tease that the franchise will end up on Xbox consoles eventually, even if it's not in the immediate future.

I put it to Holly Longdale: Is World of Warcraft: Forever launching as a PC-exclusive a missed opportunity?

"What you just described is really what we're after. Play it wherever you want and, at some point,on whatever you want. But the first leg of that journey is getting gamepads working really well with World of Warcraft, and we thought Forever was the perfect place to start. Looking at where things are going when we hear about Project Helix et cetera, I think platforms will be a bit more ubiquitous," says Longdale.

As you can see, the WoW VP teases Xbox Project Helix in her reply here, suggesting that bringing World of Warcraft to a device that already supports PC games will make things much easier for Blizzard in the future.

Still, she clearly also states that the idea is to eventually allow for World of Warcraft "on whatever you want", and the first step is to implement gamepad support that works "really well". Later in the interview, she also mentions that the work on controllers will allow players "flexibility that I think goes beyond consoles".

We'll have to wait and see what happens, but all signs are pointing towards a future where we'll be playing World of Warcraft on an Xbox console eventually - it might not be the Series X or S, but it should at least be on Project Helix.

#4131. Review: Marvel's Guardians Of The Galaxy: Encore Edition (Switch 2) - A Bright And Charming Adventure With An Okay Port

Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy: Encore Edition

While cloud streaming has its benefits, nothing beats having a native version of a game. Guardians of the Galaxy launched on the first Nintendo Switch as a Cloud version, and that experience wasn’t really recommended. Now, the game is having an Encore Edition on Switch 2 with an actual port. It’s the same fun adventure, but with some performance caveats.

Guardians of the Galaxy follows Peter Quill as Star-Lord, as he travels the galaxy with his ragtag team of heroes: Rocket Raccoon, Drax, Groot, and Gamora. It starts out as a scrappy adventure of them trying to get out of debt, but eventually becomes much more engrossing and deeper as it progresses. It’s a story about friendship and teamwork that hits all the right notes.

As someone whose immediate frame of reference for this group is the Marvel Cinematic Universe rather than the comic books, I actually enjoyed this incarnation rather than their portrayal in the movies. The voice acting, script, and art direction are top-notch.

I already played the game once before on a different platform, but revisiting on Switch 2 felt like seeing an old friend again. I laughed at the interactions and jokes, as well as getting teary-eyed at the emotional scenes, as if witnessing them for the first time.

Unsurprisingly, the graphics have taken a small hit on Switch 2 compared to other platforms, but the gorgeous environmental and enemy designs more than make up for it. The different planets are alien, yet colourful, while enemy types are more plentiful than you’d think. From weird worms to gelatinous cubes, there’s enough wackiness to keep your eyes entertained.

While you only control Peter and his dual pistols during gameplay, you can deliver attack commands to the rest of the crew. For example, Drax can stagger bigger enemies while Rocket can clear huge areas with his explosives if you’re starting to get overwhelmed. It’s a little disappointing that you can’t play as other characters, but they all feel like they’re participating in some way.

Peter also unlocks different elemental shots throughout the campaign, giving him even more options. The Ice shot freezes foes in place, allowing you to inflict even more damage, while the Lightning shot can ricochet between nearby enemies. The combat isn’t particularly deep, but there’s more than enough variation to keep things fresh.

When building up a gauge, you can activate Huddle, where Peter gives a pep talk to his teammates to bolster their spirits. If you provide the correct response based on their mood, the whole team gets a temporary strength boost. Even if you pick incorrectly, Peter himself still gets the boost. This is also a clever way to show off the game’s fantastic soundtrack, filled with classic '70s and '80s jams like Rick Astley’s Never Gonna Give You Up and Europe’s The Final Countdown. The game is already bursting with charm and personality, and the music is the perfect cherry on top.

One of Peter’s many unlockable perks is an active-reload mechanic popularised by Gears of War. If you time your button presses correctly, Peter will reload immediately instead of having to wait, making it a satisfying minigame within the hectic combat. While my preferred way to play most Switch 2 games is with a Pro Controller, the constant rumbling when firing and the active-reload feel absolutely incredible on Joy-Con, and I eventually shifted to mainly playing with them.

The Switch 2 version includes two new control schemes in Gyroscope and Mouse Mode. The former lets you tilt your controller when you’re flying the group’s spaceship, the Milano, as well as guide Peter when he’s sliding or using his Jet Boots. The latter is just as you’d expect: you can use the right Joy-Con as a mouse to move the camera. There are no surprises here.

There are also new glam-rock-inspired skins for each of the main characters. I guess it’s a nice exclusive for the Encore Edition, but doesn’t impact the overall game.

This Switch 2 port’s performance is just…fine. While docked, the quality and performance modes target 30fps and 40fps, respectively. In handheld, it targets 30fps. Even in docked mode, there are hitches and stutters throughout the campaign. The loading times aren’t great either, and I booted up my PlayStation version from 2021 to compare. On that and the Switch 2, both loading screens last roughly 15 seconds, which can be quite annoying and noticeable. The bar is very low, but performance overall is still miles better than the Cloud version!

Also, credit where it's due, the Encore Edition has squished out a few bugs and glitches. A nasty one from other platforms was that certain conversations wouldn’t trigger when picking up collectibles if you decided to load up a previous save file. Thus the items wouldn’t show up in Peter’s glossary, which was a huge problem for completionists, and the feasible solution was to start a new game. After some testing, it seems like this particular glitch has thankfully been fixed in this version.

Guardians of the Galaxy was criminally overlooked when it first came out on other platforms. This single-player adventure is full of heart with equally fun gameplay to match. It’s also a shame that the disastrous Cloud version on the first Switch cast a large shadow on an otherwise stellar release.

But those dark days are over. If you can stomach some performance issues, this is one bright and resonating story you’ll want to experience at least once. Without the need of a constant internet connection, you can take Guardians of the Galaxy: Encore Edition outside in the sun, literally!

#4130. A Line Held Tight is a charcoal visual novel about a miner's strike in the 32nd century and choosing your relationships wisely

We've had about roughly four decades of games as we generally know them now, and yet somehow, so often their stories feel so limited in scope. I'm not talking about a lack of big, bold ideas, in fact there might be too many of those. I more mean that there are aspects to life that often go uncovered in games. For example, when was the last time you saw a game about a workers strike? Citizen Sleeper 2 has one questline about such a thing, but it's just what the entire game is about. A Line Held Tight, a mecha visual novel about a sci-fi miner's strike, may bridge that gap.

A Line Held Tight is being developed by Humble Grove, the studio behind the quiet but impactful No Longer Home. Narrative is at the forefront with this game too, albeit with an emphasis on the choices you make throughout the strike. You play as The Canary, a member of a mining colony who's been cut off by the rest of humanity, set in the 32nd century. "As a strike boils over you’ll help The Canary to decide where their heart and their loyalties lie," the game's Steam page explains. "A branching narrative weaves its way through the deep tunnels of the mine to meet the characters within it as outside influences make themselves felt."

Those aforementioned choices you make primarily affect The Canary's relationships with friends, family and other workers, a much more appealing concept mechanically than simply different endings or storylines. In the world of labour organising, it's the relationships you build with others that's really the key thing, so it's nice to see an emphasis on that both narratively and mechanically. The game has some pretty stunning hand-drawn charcoal art too, as well as a traditional folk soundtrack, a pretty unique combo for a game.

As it stands, A Line Held Tight doesn't currently have a release date. Where it makes up for that is a demo that you can try out right now as part of Steam Next Fest, at the very least. There's a nice little video talking through some of the thought process of making a game such as this one from Humble Grove that you can check out below too. And while you're doing that, whether you check out the demo or not, perhaps give the game a little wishlist on Steam.

#4129. Xbox Suddenly Has Two Vice City Games Releasing In Mid-November

This one's based on Zelda with GTA influences!

What do you do if you've got a GTA-inspired game set to release around the same time as GTA 6? You schedule it for the day before, of course! That's exactly what's happening in the case of Vice: Magic City Mayhem.

This game is officially coming to Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S on November 18th, 2026 - a day before the release of GTA 6 on November 19th. As you can see, Vice: Magic City Mayhem goes all-in on the same style of artwork as the Rockstar Games epic, but the game itself couldn't really be more different.

Instead, Vice: Magic City Mayhem is described as a "top-down 8-bit retro action/adventure game inspired by Zelda with a Vice City theme". It essentially seems like what you'd get if you took old-school Zelda and combined it with Vice City.

Step into the shoes of Dutch, one of Magic City’s most feared enforcers, on a thrilling and dangerous quest to rescue your one true love, Sophie. Navigate through the chaos of wild nightclubs, scenic beaches, and raptor-infested yachts in this raunchy, high-stakes adventure.

In Vice: Magic City Mayhem, we blend the best of both worlds—drawing inspiration from the immersive exploration, intense combat, and mind-bending puzzles of Zelda, alongside the outrageous storylines, vibrant world-building, and dark humor of Vice City.

What's particularly interesting about this is that it started life as a Kickstarter project last year, securing $13,278 worth of funding alongside a $10,000 goal. Some of the developers working on the project have worked at the likes of EA and Telltale Games as well, so there's every chance it's going to be worth picking up.

Let's see how it goes, eh? We just admire the bravery of releasing right next to GTA 6 in November with a game that seems similar but actually offers something very different, and here's hoping that bold bet will ultimately pay off.

If you're interested, Vice: Magic City Mayhem is available to pre-order on the Xbox Store for £12.49 / $14.99.

Roam the gritty streets of Magic City, facing off against a colorful, eccentric cast of enemies and bosses, all while chasing down your elusive "Princess" in a city where danger is around every corner. It’s an unforgettable ride filled with heart-pounding action, clever puzzles, and plenty of ridiculous humor - perfect for anyone looking to save the day with style!

#4128. Rumour: Days Gone Dev to Announce and Launch New PS5 Game in 2027

Third-person game with co-op, it's reported

Bend Studio, the first-party team best known for Days Gone, plans to reveal and potentially even release its next game in 2027.

That's according to a new MP1st report, which shares more details on the project. The outlet claims an announcement will take place next year and it's "much further along in development" than you might think, so much so that Bend Studio is also planning to release it in 2027.

MP1st calls the project a third-person experience with co-op features, but it's not a live service title.

The website also claims it won't be a sequel to Days Gone. Previous reports stated Bend Studio pitched a Days Gone 2 to Sony after the first game, but it was turned down. It then actually did turn its attention to a Game as a Service, though this was cancelled at the start of last year.

Now, according to the outlet, Bend Studio is gearing up to announce and release its project next year. With Until Dawn 2, God of War Laufey, and potentially also Intergalactic slated for 2027, it could be a busy 12 months for Sony's first-party developers.

This is just the latest report from MP1st surrounding PlayStation's unannounced plans. It has also suggested a Killzone project is in the works, and teased what to expect from Media Molecule next.

Rumour Killzone Project in Early Development, Probably a Remake

Rumour Media Molecule's Next Game Is Out Next Year and Unlike Anything It's Made Before

With a new PS5 title around the corner, Bend Studio is indeed best known for Days Gone, as its biggest and most recent project. However, the developer has been part of Sony for over 20 years. In that time, it also made tons of Syphon Filter games, Resistance: Retribution for PSP, and Uncharted: Golden Abyss on the PS Vita.

With a Days Gone sequel ruled out, what do you hope Bend Studio is working on? Let us know in the comments below.

#4127. Cyberpunk 2077's new dual wielding has already been modded to include shotguns and rifles, provided you're down to get "janky and wildly overpowered"

It was only ever going to be a matter of time, but I'm still surprised just how quickly Cyberpunk 2077 modders have taken pistol dual wielding mechanic the RPG's Edgerunners 2 update has just added in, and opened it up to include any gun Night City has to offer. Yep, twinning shotguns, assault rifles, sniper rifles, or any combo of those is now possible. Though, you'll have to make peace with the fact enemies will struggle to match your firepower.

A number of different modders instantly decided to take on the task of extending the tag which governs Cyberpunk's new dual wielding perk to include everything with a trigger. There's Dual Wield Anything by long-time Cyberpunk modder E3roKK, Dual Wield Anything and Everything for 2.5 by Jollywankers, and Expanded Dual Wielding by JericoHellden. All three have been released within the last 24 hours.

JericoHellden's mod also includes the option to control each gun separately, rather than CD Projekt Red's default of automatically alternating between the two when firing. If you're only interested in twinning pistols, but do want the ability to independently fire each gun, another new mod - Independent Pistol Controls (Dual Wielding) by Dederara - might be for you.

Here are clips showing Jollywankers' (directly below) and Dederara's (the further down of the two) works in action:

It's worth noting that, in line with the reason CD Projekt Red gave for limiting it to pistols in their official update, dual wielding other guns without any measures in place to make enemies tougher does blunt the challenge of fighting your way through Night City. JericoHellden declared it a "janky and wildly overpowered" experience, and E3roKK made clear that anyone expecting animations not to get a bit clippy or awkward at times is barking up the wrong tree.

If you're hoping to dual wield katanas, unfortunately it looks like melee weapons will take a bit more time to figure out properly, with some of these mods including them only as a 'try it but don't expect things to work yet' afterthought to the ranged main course. Makes sense, given the official integration is designed for lead slingers rather than slappy cybersticks.

The latest version of Cyber Engine Tweaks, the framework mod needed for any Cybeprunk mod setup that's not limited to the likes of light visual tweaks, is a requirement for all for of the mods mentioned here. Redscript is also needed for Expanded Dual Wielding.

#4126. Forza Horizon 6 explodes on Steam even before it's officially out

Forza Horizon 6 looks to have easily delivered the most successful launch for any game in the series on PC, with record-breaking player numbers.

Steam is abuzz this week with a couple of long-anticipated launches, but in Forza Horizon 6’s case, at least, the game isn’t even out for what will be most of its players. The anticipated sequel in the open-world driving game series doesn’t officially launch until May 19, but owners of its most expensive version - the Premium Edition - can play it right now.

That version of the game includes more than just a few days of early access, of course, but you’d think the $120 price tag would’ve only been palatable to a small group of players. Not the case with this game.

Forza Horizon 6, which has spent 16 weeks in Steam’s global top sellers list, currently occupies the number two spot, having jumped up three spots this week in anticipation of the launch. The game has also naturally been popular with players, so popular in fact that it has already overtaken the player counts of all other Horizon games on the platform.

At the time of writing, the game has peaked at 128,157 concurrent players on Steam alone (via SteamDB). The figure has already climbed several times during the writing of this story, so you can only imagine how much higher it’s going to get deeper into the weekend.

All of that, of course, days before the official launch on Tuesday, when, theoretically, the majority of the game’s audience will be able to start playing. In just a few short hours, Horizon 6 has already gone well above Forza Horizon 5’s peak concurrent of 81,096, as well as Forza Horizon 4’s peak 75,689 players.

Steam is the only platform that publishes player numbers, of course, but it’s easy to see how similar the enthusiasm is going to be on Xbox. Though the game is not yet part of the Game Pass line-up, those who don’t want to wait could buy the Premium Edition Upgrade to get the included content, and play it right now.

Game Pass, and Xbox / Windows Store numbers don’t factor into Steam’s, which is another thing to consider when viewing the numbers holistically. Indeed, given how successful Forza Horizon 5 has been on PlayStation 5, Horizon 6’s upcoming release on Sony's console is bound to be even bigger.

Forza Horizon 5 has been off to a similarly flying start in the first few days of its own advanced access launch, so it’s obviously not surprising to see Horizon 6 do better there. In case you missed it, check out our review of Forza Horizon 6. In short, we really liked it, even if we expected more.

#4125. Review: Stellar Blade: Complete Edition (Switch 2) - Perfectly Playable, Despite Drawbacks

Though the genre has evolved and deepened over time, gacha games have historically not been praised for their depth and complexity, often being criticised for being thinly veiled gambling machines. People were understandably incredulous, then, when Shift Up — the studio behind Goddess of Victory: Nikke — announced in 2019 that it would pursue a AAA passion project called Stellar Blade. Even more were then shocked a few years later when this wildly different, ambitious project turned out to be a pretty solidly made action game.

Stellar Blade has now been ported to Switch 2 (along with some cheeky new cosmetic Bayonetta DLC), bringing this titillating and gripping action experience to the Nintendo audience. It hasn’t made the transition to more modest hardware completely unscathed, but this is nonetheless a solidly enjoyable and thrilling adventure that deserves a spot in your library.

The narrative is set in the distant, post-apocalypse future, when our planet has been overrun by monstrous creatures called Naytibas. Some humans escaped after losing the war and established a space-based orbital colony called…the Colony…from which occasional squadrons of elite super-soldiers are deployed to attempt to regain a foothold on Earth.

Protagonist Eve is a member of one of these squads and the prologue opens with her landing mission, a violent meatgrinder reminiscent of the Omaha Beach scene in Saving Private Ryan in which she’s seemingly the sole warrior who survives. Aided by a mysterious man who saved her, Eve sets out to track down the Alpha Naytiba and hopefully notch a win for the humans.

It’s a decently entertaining story, but one which feels a little surface-level in many ways. Characters — Eve included — lack depth and converse in a stilted way that sounds as if they’re quoting lines at each other, and some of the later plot twists are the sort of thing that you can see coming a mile away. Yet there’s just enough lore here to keep you interested in the setting and Eve’s ongoing journey and occasional moments of levity help to keep things from feeling too dour.

Any disappointment with the storytelling is quickly forgotten by the thrill of combat, which feels like a cross between a Soulslike and a character action game as Eve deftly combos enemies with her athletic acrobatics and expert sword strikes.

Enemies hit hard and fast and can easily stunlock you, meaning that even a single average foe can take quite a large chunk out of your health bar if you're not paying careful attention and multiple foes at once can rapidly overwhelm Eve due to limited mobility and crowd control options.

Along with the usual combos you can string together with light and heavy attacks, Eve also has a variety of limited-use Beta Skills she can use to turn the tide in her favour. You build up Beta Energy from attacks and perfectly timed blocks or parries, and this energy can then be burned mid-combo to either bolster an attack or use a flashy guard-breaking attack that can put the enemy on the back foot. This system adds a nice bit of room for player skill expression, as you can find some creative ways to weave together combos and Beta Skills to positively melt foes.

Though even common enemies can put you to the test in certain configurations, this combat system really sings when you get to one of the many cinematic boss fights against powerful, grotesque monsters. These act as occasional hard skill checks that will forcibly teach you deeper knowledge of combat mechanics as you carefully study their movesets for brief gaps and learn (often across multiple failed attempts) how to best exploit those gaps with your available tools.

Eve thus feels both all-powerful and vulnerable at the same time, which lends combat encounters a thrilling and electric feel as you oscillate between slicing enemies to ribbons with practised cinematic flair and getting absolutely folded when you mis-time a dodge. Practice makes perfect, and there's lots of satisfaction that comes from progressing across the hours and going up against increasingly more complicated and dangerous foes with sharpened reflexes and skill.

Yet progress happens in more ways than just raw skill development - there are also some light RPG elements that allow you to slowly shape Eve's build over time. Not only can you use skill points to unlock and power up new combat abilities and Beta Skills, but you can also improve stats like max health and attack through finding collectibles in the environment.

Gear can also be found and crafted to give Eve certain passive buffs, allowing you to get more value out of the playstyle you generally choose. These RPG mechanics help to soften some of the harder edges of the often unforgiving combat system, giving you meaningful ways to progress over time even if you struggle greatly with losing battles to enemies.

World and level design initially follows traditional Soulslike tropes, consisting of lots of claustrophobic halls and labyrinthine paths that often loop back on each other with unlocked doors and ladders that lead back to the nearest checkpoint. While the critical path is usually obvious and easy to follow, there are often a handful of side areas to explore along the way rife with more platforming gauntlets, challenging enemy placements and extra upgrades and goodies. This design does a great job of rewarding exploration while keeping you moving forward.

Then, roughly six or so hours in, things change up with the sudden introduction of a medium-sized open-world area, filled with quests, collectibles, and points of interest to scour. Travelling between this area and a nearby hub has both gameplay and narrative benefits, as you complete quests and bounties to progress various side storylines for NPCs living there and find increasingly better gear and unlockables as quest and exploration rewards.

It admittedly seems at first like a weird left turn after the opening hours set very different expectations, but ultimately feels like a worthy addition to the gameplay loop. And even after its introduction, there are plenty of returns to the more focused and level-based Soulslike design, which balances out the free but occasionally meandering levels and quests that can come with the open world.

Graphics look decent, but not exceptional, due in part to both the overall art direction and the Switch 2’s relatively modest hardware. Some of the vistas of the ruined Earth can be quite nice to look at from afar, but there’s a lot of muted colours utilised as you trawl through tunnels, sewers, deserts, and destroyed office buildings. Environments thus tend to blend together and often lack visually interesting landmarks or set pieces, which can make the sections more focused on exploration a little more dull.

Meanwhile, the game outputs at 720p handheld and 1080p docked, which can lead to visuals that look even more muddy due to the upscaling artifacting and relatively low internal resolutions.

Regarding performance, everything technically runs at 60fps, but there's a pretty massive caveat with that claim: this frame rate is only accomplished through frame generation. Practically speaking, this means that there's a significant amount of input lag despite the visuals themselves appearing to animate smoothly. For a game this focused on quick reaction times and granular movement, that input lag can be a death knell and does noticeably reduce the playability of this port.

However, there is an option in the settings to turn this off and reduce the game to what appears to be closer to 40fps, which feels like a much more acceptable compromise. Controls are quite a bit more responsive here, while the frame rate is noticeably smoother than 30fps. There are some drops that can still happen when panning the camera around in larger areas, but it doesn’t overly affect the playability of combat encounters and this becomes less of an issue in the many smaller environments.

All this is to say, Stellar Blade is a game that appears to be stretching the Switch 2 to its limits, but it’s a perfectly playable and often surprisingly good-looking port that accurately brings this impressive game to a lightweight handheld.

It can sometimes feel easier to pick apart a port for its flaws and what it lacks, and while there are valid critiques here to be made about the sometimes disappointing visuals and performance, it’s hard to get away from the fact that this is a ‘good enough’ version of Stellar Blade that you can play wherever you want to take your console.

Despite some drawbacks, Stellar Blade stands tall as an impressive and enjoyable action game that occupies a nice niche in the Switch 2 library. Rewarding exploration, thrilling combat, and tough but fair difficulty carry this game far and make it an easy recommendation, even if its story can be a bit bland and the visuals aren’t always up to the task.

I’d recommend this to anyone looking for a higher-budget game that favours exploration and combat; Stellar Blade excels in its implementation of both and makes a great first impression as Shift Up’s entrance into AAA game development.

@AussieMcBucket I see where you're coming from and this is something I often keep in mind as I write about bigger third party projects like this. In my experience, there's often a difference between AAA games that were obviously designed for much beefier target hardware and games that either are lightweight or were explicitly designed for Nintendo hardware.

For games in the former category, they CAN be made to run on something like the Switch 2, but various visual cuts have to be made that compromise the original art direction in subtle, but often meaningful ways. For something like Resident Evil 3, these compromises are so small that they're largely irrelevant and lead to a port that's indistinguishable unless you want to really split hairs. But for Stellar Blade, there are many areas where the blurry textures or inconsistent frame rates often remind me in an unfavorable way that this hardware can't completely deliver on the game's original vision.

I'll be upfront that this game looks and performs 'good enough' for me--I have the PS5 version and got about 20 hours into it, but I'll be continuing my new save on Switch 2 and finishing it there because I just prefer the portability more and the visual drawbacks don't really get in the way of my enjoyment of it.

But when I write a review for a game like this, I think I'd be misrepresenting the product to our readers if I didn't bracket my own preferences and at least highlight the ways in which it distinctly falls short of the visual fidelity of other ports, if there are any such notable differences.

All of which is to say, at least in my reviews, I try not to lean too hard into pixel counting and fixating on all the way in which other ports are better. I appreciate your feedback, though, and think it's important to keep in mind that many games ultimately just need to be fun to play, even if they don't look perfect.

#4124. Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.3 will take us deeper into the World in Canvas and make Mortenax Blade playable

Honkai: Star Rail's next big outing will see the continuation of the Planarcadia story, and it's going to be with us soon.

HoYoverse has today delivered full details on the next major update for Honkai: Star Rail. Version 4.3, dubbed The Lethe Below the Living, will be available for all players on June 1. The upcoming update adds a new chapter to the Planarcadia arc, and introduce a new playable character.

The new narrative chapter will also unveil more about Mortenax Blade, the Trailblazer themselves, and the husk of the Aeon.

Mortenax Blade is the hero of this chapter, and he’s going to step into the World in Canvas. The goal is to - by borrowing the power of Voracity - excise Shuhu from his body and end the curse.

The Trailblazer goes on a trip of their own in Version 4.3, this time to Inkford Hermitage, right on the edge between the World in Canvas and the real world. They’re going to undertake this journey to warn Graphia of the Asat Pramad threat.

In case you hadn’t already guessed, Mortenax Blade is this version’s new playable character. The 5-Star Fire-Type swordsman is on the Path of Nihility. Blade’s Ultimate allows him to enter an enhanced state by deploying a special Bounded Field.

While the field is active, all enemies receive more DMG. Entering this state is also how Blade unlocks his skill, which uses a Sword Formation to deal more damage. This is then used to essentially unlock a second, more powerful Ultimate for him.

The benefits of Mortenax Blade’s kit extend to his teammates, too. Any ally who attacks an enemy with him on the team, they inflict a debuff on them. This also builds up a special Charge that Blade can later use with his Skill.

Version 4.3’s launch arrives alongside the Gift of Tempered Blade event. Through it, you can claim a new Trailblazer Outfit piece for free, but only after getting Mortenax Blade from Warping. The first phase’s rerun will be Yao Guang, and the second phase will bring back both Cyrene and Phainon.

You can also expect the Wispae Amusement Park to arrive within the World in Canvas, which you’ll get to design. You can plan where the rides will go, pick the different themes, set visitor routes and more.

Starward Mode is another new addition, which can be found in Memory of Chaos, Pure Fiction, and Apocalyptic Shadow. Starward will see you take on three different stages, which you’ll need three teams for. Clearing each challenge with full stars will reward you 100 Stellar Jades extra per chase.

There’s more coming down the line, too. A new Fate/Stay Night [Unlimited Blade Works] collaboration will arrive in a content up this summer. The event will give players a chance to earn Gilgamesh or Archer for free by logging in.

#4122. "What if Larian had shut down after Divine Divinity?": Star Trek Online exec scorns publishers who close teams like BioWare in favour of "AAA veteran" start-ups and AI "magic beans"

It's like "setting fire to millions of dollars of property and equipment"

Breaking up established game development teams in favour of "AAA veteran" start-ups and "magic bean" technologies is like "setting fire to millions of dollars of property and equipment", in the words of Star Trek Online executive producer Thomas Marrone. He thinks it's "wildly irresponsible and self-sabotaging", and that videogame company shareholders should be absolutely furious about it.

Marrone's comments come in response to EA closing BioWare yesterday, but he takes aim at closures and layoffs across the industry. He notes that many of the most successful teams owe their accomplishments to lessons learned from screw-ups, and suggests that if big game publishers just want "number to go up", they should get out of the game-making trade and pour all their cash into investment funds.

"One of the most insightful comments about game development came from a former boss," Marrone wrote on Bluesky this morning. "He said 'Making a game is like starting a band. You can’t throw money at a new studio with random AAA veterans and expect it to crank out a hit.' A good game needs a vision. A good game needs a good team to build it. A good team needs chemistry to work well together. Team chemistry needs years of collaboration to gel. There are certainly 'rockstars' and leaders who are anchors for their team, but they need to have that chemistry and trust with everyone around them to be truly effective.

"The AAA philosophy seems to be to hire four random musicians and expect them to become the Beatles overnight," Marrone went on. "When it does happen: well, we have the songs now, we can just hire different musicians to record new songs when we want another album. It’s truly insane and shows a fundamental misunderstanding of the collaborative creative process at the heart of making games.

"Most studios that generate an overnight hit are actually on the 3rd or 4th title," he said. "Blizzard, Larian, Arrowhead, these places had several games under their belts before their first true blockbuster. Like George RR Martin they had been grinding XP for years before becoming a household name. The current AAA Publisher practice of disbanding studios, even if they ship a game successfully, is so counterintuitive to their own financial future it boggles my mind.

"Like if I were a major shareholder I would be livid," Marrone observed. "This is wanton destruction of these publishers’ most precious assets. It’s like literally setting fire to millions of dollars of property and equipment. It’s wildly irresponsible and self-sabotaging. If big game publishers just want number to go up, fire everyone and just invest it all in mutual funds or something. If you don’t want to actually make a product, and you don’t want to build a business around making a product, just liquidate your assets and stop pretending you want to make anything."

Marrone has been at Cryptic Studios for 16 years, starting out as an associate graphics designer. "I've worked on one game through that whole career, which means I've seen lots of leaders come and go, and lots of versions of the company and the game as it grew, shrunk, and changed," he noted.

Cryptic themselves were founded in 2000, and are also known for Champions Online, City of Heroes and Neverwinter. They've been through a lot of upheaval lately. Cryptic were acquired by (*dread bell tolls*) publishing conglomerate Embracer in 2021, during the latter's early-Covid-era campaign to absorb half the industry. When Embracer belatedly acknowledged that all of their acquisitions had left them up shit creek without a paddle, Cryptic Studios were among the many subsidiaries who had to lay off staff. Then, Embracer sold them to Project Golden Arc, a new company formed by former Star Trek Online publishers Arc and XD Inc, publishers of Torchlight: Infinite and Heartopia.

I'm not sure how many of Cryptic's founding staff are still there, but Marrone makes it sound like they've done a fair job of keeping their teams together. "I have very personal experience working on a team that has gone through all the corpo speak stages 'forming, storming, norming, and performing,'" he wrote. "It can take Y E A R S to get to that final stage. When you do, it's awesome. People are 2, 3, 4x as effective as when they start. But it just. takes. Time."

"It takes time to build a team," Marrone went on. "It takes shared experiences. It takes shared wins AND shared losses. What if Larian had shut down after Divine Divinity? What if Arrowhead had shut down after Magicka? What if Hello Games had shuttered after the initial launch of No Man's Sky? These studios have all had ups and downs but they were given time to grow and learn and their teams got better and better. Not to say those teams were static, but certainly there was a continuity and culture that informed their biggest successes.

"And when you look at the arc of a studio like Bioware, you can begin to see how important it is to keep the teams healthy, how important it is to keep those rockstars and leaders together with the teams that know them," he said. "Mass Effect is a great game. Mass Effect 2 is one of the best games of all time.

"In my current position I understand the pressure of leadership when millions of dollars and hundreds of salaries are at stake," Marrone concluded. "I understand the drive to find a magic bean like NFTs or GenAI or whatever is trending on LinkedIn this week. There's got to be a 'trick.' We've got to find a 'trick.' But." Marrone ends the thread by reiterating the need to "nurture and empower your team".

We've heard plenty of common-sensical commentary like this from other senior devs of late. In April, Bit Reactor boss and former XCOM developer Greg Foertsch spoke to Julian about how he and other Firaxis managers "kept the team together" across development of Sid Meier's Railroads, XCOM: Enemy Unknown, and XCOM 2.

We've also recently seen a number of new "AAA veteran" startups come and go, as investors take fright after an initial buzz of interest during the Covid lockdown period. Former BioWare manager Casey Hudson launched a new studio in 2021 only to shutter the company in 2024. Former Mass Effect and Dragon Age scribe Mac Walters similarly launched a company in 2023, only for publishers NetEase to pull funding a year later. There are going to be a lot more BioWare veterans in the wilds this year, joining many thousands laid off by the likes of Microsoft and Ubisoft.

#4121. Rumour: Alleged Persona 1 Remake Gameplay Leaks Online

Alleged footage of a Persona 1 Remake has emerged online, although in this age of AI generated content it’s incredibly difficult to ascertain whether this is legit or not.

My jerk reaction is that it’s probably real, as it appears to include reused animations from the unreleased Persona 4 Revival. A similar leak occurred prior to the official announcement of Persona 3 Reload.

But as always, you should take this with a pinch of salt.

The video shows combat featuring characters from Persona 1, alongside Persona 2’s protagonist Tatsuya Suou.

Series producer Kazuhisa Wada has spoken quite candidly about how Persona 1 and 2 remakes are something Atlus should “eventually do”, so this project has been an open secret for some time now.

It’s worth noting that Persona 4 Revival is due out on 17th February, so even if this footage is real, I wouldn’t expect two remakes in the same year. It’s probably still a little way away.

News 'It's Like Cultural Preservation': Persona Producer Mentions Persona 1 and 2 Remakes Yet Again

News 'I Think We Have to Do It': Persona 1 and 2 Remakes Sound More Likely Than Ever

As the Editor of Push Square, Sammy has over 15 years of experience analysing the world of PlayStation, from PS3 through PS5 and everything in between. He’s an expert on PS Studios and industry matters, as well as sports games and simulators. He also enjoys RPGs when he has the time to dedicate to them, and is a bit of a gacha whale.

The Tatsuya bit is pretty weird, but can be brushed off as a placeholder, especially if we consider they're also planning remaking P2's duology (why wouldn't they at that point?).

It also screams early investor showcase video with how it's broken down. Not the first time a Sega investor video was leaked - a few years back we got our first look at the Sonic Frontiers beta, P3 Reload and the new Jet Set Radio from one of these leaks.

I'm leaning towards real, but this is probably at least two years away from releasing, 2027 is P4R and likely P6, so late 2028 at minimum. Persona 1 doesn't have the modern Persona formula with the social SIM aspects spread over a year so it'll be a shorter game to remake. You can beat the original in less than 40 hours.

It has a 70s anime feel. So stylish and atmospheric. Hoping it's real!

#4120. Monopoly Go x The Simpsons crossover is almost here

After a long wait and exhaustive leaks, the highly-anticipated Simpsons event will finally arrive in Monopoly Go very soon, alongside new content.

Monopoly Go players have been looking forward to a major crossover event for what felt like months, and though most of the details ended up leaking, nothing actually beats official information.

The world of The Simpsons has officially arrived in Monopoly Go, and there's a whole lot for players to dive into. The show's creative team even produced a new animated short, featuring Mr. Monopoly, and Mr. Burns.

Available June 3 through July 29, the new event allows Monopoly Go players to jump in the world of The Simpsons. You'll be able to build, and explore all around multiple iconic locations from the show.

Along the way, you'll run into Simpsons characters like Homer, Marge, Bart, Lisa, and of course, Mr. Burns. Developer Scopely teamed up with the show's creative team to create many references, and Easter Eggs for you to discover. You'll find some of those on chance cards, but most of the world has been changed to be part of The Simpsons, including getting to bribe Chief Wiggum to escape jail.

The developer promises a deeply connected world with Simpsons narratives and characters that alter seasonal maps, and offer unique sticker sets and animated sequences to dive in. Incidentally, this is The Simpsons' first appearance in a mobile-exclusive game in 13 years.

Here's a breakdown of everything you can expect, straight from Scopely:

Episodes: Narrative-driven encounters that create stories inspired by The Simpsons. Episodes play out across seasonal boards, sticker sets, and minigames, all capped off with an animated short.

Sticker sets: Every Episode comes with its own limited-time sticker set, taking cues from the latest Simpsons story. Collectible artwork, character journeys and other rewards are yours to claim for the duration of each Episode.

The Simpsons Run: Every two weeks, a new Springfield character will take over the Free Parking tile, kicking off character-driven runs.

Simpsons-themed Shutdowns and Heists: Monopoly Go's shutdowns and heists get a Simpsons makeover, with Springfield-inspired chaos and disasters.

Bribe Wiggum: This changes Go to Jail to allow players to bribe Chief Wiggum, giving you a chance to earn a bigger reward, but not without introducing an element of unpredictability.

Simpsons chance cards: The chance card collection grows with over 50 Simpsons-themed cards full of memes, references and one-liners from the show.

If you're excited to jump in tomorrow, be sure to check out these Free Monopoly Go Dice Links before you dive into the new content.

#4119. Half-Life 3 speculation reignited by Valve dev mentioning three sweet little rumored codenamey letters amid technical chat about video game noises

Wake up. There's Half-Life 3 chatter occurring again. This time because, about an hour into a panel about sounds in video games, a Valve composer has uttered three eyebrow-raising letters. HLX. In an industry rife with acronyms, what's so special about this one? Well, it's a rumoured codename for the next entry in the aforementioned series about a man with a crowbar, for one.

"Basically, that's one of the three pieces that come together to make HDR that you can easily optimise," Valve music designer Mike Morasky said during a panel at GameSoundCon, answering a regular old question about the techincal ins and out of managing sound in games. The panel had been running for about an hour when he said this, so clearly nothing that'd get people out of their seats was in the offing.

"In fact, I think Deadlock has their own version of HDR," he continued. "HLX has its own version, so on and so forth." AHA, voices screamed around the world. He said the thing. HLX, in case you're not on top of the list of acronyms that should set you off yapping about Valve games, previously appeared in a data string from a Counter-Strike 2 update and looks like it could turn out to be a codename for a future game from Gabe and co. That's going off Half-Life: Alyx's codename having been HLVR.

If it was HLXXX, I imagine one would have to assume it to be a possible codename for a Gordon Freeman sex tape or a Half-Life collaboration with Vin Diesel, star of the 2002 film XXX. I don't know about you, but either would excite me greatly.

Morasky's co-panelist David Feise doesn't look to have been subtle in sarcastically pointing out the former's slip of the tongue to him via some cheeky whispering while the two were still up in stage. Morasky also looks to have plenty of form for this sort of tongue slippage in relation to HLX.

Does any of this tell us anything other than potentially confirming once more that Half-Life 3 exists? No, but hey, it's something. One thing we do know is that ex-Valve writer Chet Faliszek has said that he wouldn't be interested in helping pen a Half-Life 3 if indeed one is hiding in the ether to catch out musicians whose mouths sometimes move faster than their brains (as happens to all of us).

#4118. Helldivers 3 "only makes sense" if it’s so unlike Helldivers 2 "that both games can exist side by side", says Arrowhead boss, discussing their new prototype game

95% of studio still on Helldivers 2, with a "small team" on the next game

Arrowhead Game Studios will only make a Helldivers 3 if it's lightyears apart in style from Helldivers 2, or if Helldivers 2's playercount falls through the floor. This is my takeaway, at least, from a recent chat with Johan Pilestedt, chief creative officer, in which Pilestedt touched briefly on the studio's next unannounced game, while assuring me that there are still no plans for a Helldiver threequel.

According to Pilestedt, 95% of the studio is focused on Helldivers 2, with a "small team" now prototyping Arrowhead's next game. They currently have around 150 people on the books. "Studio-wise, we want to grow on our own terms and know when to stop," Pilestedt commented over email, noting that "plenty of teams hit big and immediately double their size".

As for the prospect of Helldivers 3, Pilestedt is wary of dividing the audience while Helldivers 2 still has a following, commenting that "for now, my view is that a sequel resets everything and forces players to start over", whereas "a continuation turns the game into a lifelong hobby, like LEGO or Warhammer". In what probably isn't a sign that he's getting David Lynch to direct the next Warbonds video, he framed Helldivers 2 "as a 'third space,' a community where people can spend a huge amount of their time, but equally one that players can go away from for months or years and still find fun and community when they come back." For context, Helldivers 2's Steam live playercount as of writing is 47,097, which isn't chart-topping but seems fairly respectable for a two-year-old game; this doesn't include console players, of course.

"Some studios can treat players like a short-term cash grab," Pilestedt went on. "We see players as the actual engine of the game: they're the ones bringing in friends, making memes, and keeping the game alive. When you have an active community doing that, you don’t need a sequel.

"The industry is panicking because the old live-service tricks don’t work anymore," he said. "And the biggest competitor to a Helldivers 3 would be Helldivers 2. It only makes sense to make a distinct sequel if it’s so different that both games can exist side by side. For now, making Helldivers 2 better every day makes way more sense than throwing away its momentum."

Pilestedt didn't spell out what he meant by the industry panicking, but I assume he's referring to all the live service game cancellations of late. 'Live service' in general – aka, turning games into platforms from which 'rents' can be extracted, be it an optional cosmetic purchase or a subscription - has become something of a cussword among players who'd rather their games were less online, habit-forming and, well, landlordy.

The intrigue here, for me, is just how different Helldivers 3 would need to be to stand apart from its predecessor. Helldivers 2 is a very different game from the original Helldivers, swapping the old top-down view for third-person gunnery with a greater emphasis on physics and credible weapon handling. Where should they go next?

I'm not sure Helldivers would be entertaining as a first-person shooter – so much of the game's beguiling daftness depends on seeing your character. I could well imagine a Helldivers RTS, but that'd probably be a spin-off project. There are other directions they could take within the third-person shooter genre that might change the feel while supporting the game's brash and callous dystopian humour. God, I almost typed the words "Helldivers battle royale" there. Close one!
